summary: Astronomical observation of Sirius.
description: questionnaire-based report describes the observation of a very bright, fixed point of light in the East on December 31, 2009, around 9:00 PM (local time). The initially described rapid and high-altitude movement of the object was actually due to cloud movement. The observation duration (10 minutes) of this very bright, fixed point changing color suggests the presence of Sirius, the brightest star in our sky. The astronomical configuration of the sky does indeed show the presence of Sirius in the observed portion of the sky (East) at the time of the observation. This is a Class A event, like the observation of Sirius.

summary: Probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: On December 31, 2009, around midnight, two groups of people observed lights moving in the sky above Contamines-Montjoie (Haute-Savoie) that quickly disappeared. Upon returning from vacation, one of the witnesses, intrigued by his observation, contacted GEIPAN and filed a report with the gendarmerie. He also detailed the characteristics of the objects observed by all the witnesses in the questionnaire. These characteristics were similar to those of Thai lanterns released during festivals. The case was classified as category B, indicating a probable sighting of flying lanterns (see the GEIPAN investigation report).

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a green light: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On December 27, 2009, at 1:00 AM, a witness observed from their window the rapid passage of an intense and continuous green light from south-northeast. No noise was noticed during the observation, which lasted a few seconds. This observation has all the characteristics of an atmospheric reentry of a meteor (meteorite), also called a bolide: a straight streak across the sky in a few seconds, with a green color. This event was not recorded by the REFORME observer network. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteor (meteorite fall).

summary: Probable sighting of flying lanterns.
description: On December 25, 2009, at 8:30 PM, a witness observed two rows of yellow lights moving across the sky. No unusual noises were heard during the approximately ten-minute observation. These lights quickly crossed the sky and disappeared to the northeast before the witness had time to take photographs. No other reports were collected. Based on the description provided, the witness likely observed Thai lanterns.

summary: Random movement of red lights above the ocean.
description: On December 19, 2009, between 8:30 p.m. and 9:30 p.m., several witnesses observed intense red lights moving over the ocean. The main witness reported five separate sightings during which he claimed to have seen the same light. This witness did not go to the local police station, and no other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon. In a letter dated June 9, 2010, the main witness informed GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimentation on Astronomy and Nuclear Safety) that his observation was of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observations of a ballet of 5 to 6 bluish light halos in the overcast sky: probable observation of light rays produced by a multi-beam projector.
description: On December 13, 2009, at approximately 11:00 PM, two people watched for a long time from their second-floor kitchen as several halos of bluish light appeared in the overcast sky. The witnesses clearly observed the beams of a multi-beam "Sky Tracer" type spotlight, whose elegant and unusual choreography deceived their vigilance. This case is classified as Class B, a probable observation of a multi-beam spotlight.

summary: Probable atmospheric re-entry.
description: On December 11, 2009, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon crossing the sky from east to west for two to three seconds, followed by a bright turquoise-blue trail. As she correctly suspected, this person likely witnessed the atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon in the sky.
description: On December 11, 2009, around 8 p.m., a person observed a white light in the sky that intrigued them. This stationary phenomenon, after an upward trajectory, was observed for 10 minutes by the witness, who took a photograph. Unfortunately, the photograph is unusable. No other witness accounts corroborate this observation, for which we lack information and details.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On December 8, 2009, between 7:20 and 7:30 a.m., a witness observed a luminous sphere in the sky for 10 to 20 seconds. Its movement was horizontal, following a west-east trajectory. This sphere disintegrated, breaking into two or three pieces before disappearing. The described phenomenon, moving horizontally at high speed and separating ("exploding") into several pieces, appears to correspond to the characteristics of atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On December 3, 2009, at approximately 10:30 PM, a motorist observed a very rapid passage of a luminous phenomenon very low in the sky. The witness described two halos of very intense light. No other reports were received regarding this phenomenon. The observation is entirely consistent with a meteor or atmospheric reentry of space debris: high brightness, high speed, and a straight trajectory. The possible double trail likely corresponds to the fragmentation of the object upon entering the atmosphere, a common occurrence.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent passage of three round, yellow lights in the sky forming a triangle.
description: On December 3, 2009, at 7:16 a.m., two high school students observed three round, yellow lights in the sky, forming a triangle. The lights moved silently and quite quickly before suddenly disappearing. GEIPAN received only one questionnaire. The witness did not respond to a request for a drawing. The written description was insufficient for GEIPAN to conduct an investigation: lack of information.

summary: Observation of movement of several bright white dots: lack of information.
description: On November 30, 2009, between 8:30 and 10:00 AM, three witnesses observed three white dots moving in a clear sky. GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) received only one witness report, describing a very long, discontinuous observation of several bright points moving in the sky. The observation was reported to GEIPAN a month later, and the witness's request for a police report was not followed up, preventing an investigation. The characteristics of the observation (very long = 1 hour 30 minutes, slow movements) could correspond to those of balloons, seagulls (present in the witness's field of vision), as suggested by the witness, or any other conceivable hypothesis, although these possibilities could not be verified. The level of strangeness is low, and the witness report is unique. This case is classified as category C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of three bright points forming a triangle.
description: person reported by telephone observing, for thirty seconds, a star that grew larger, followed by the silent, steady passage of three luminous points forming a triangle. The phenomenon quickly disappeared in the direction of Figeac. The observation of a growing (approaching) "star" and three luminous points in a triangle could correspond to an aircraft (air corridor), but despite repeated requests from GEIPAN (the French UFO research group), the witness has not provided any information (no questionnaire, no official report). Any investigation is therefore impossible.

summary: Probable observation of the ISS passing followed by the space shuttle Alantis.
description: On November 26, 2009, at 6:35 PM, a witness observed two large, intrigued points of light in the sky. For six to seven minutes, the witness noted a particular intensity of light and the absence of flashing lights or any noise associated with the event. The points followed each other at a slow and constant speed. No other similar sightings were reported. After verification, it is highly probable that the witness's observation was of the International Space Station (ISS) followed by the Space Shuttle Atlantis during mission STS-129.

summary: Observation of the silent passage across the night sky of a dozen objects with a central light: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On November 26, 2009, at approximately 10:45 PM, two people were surprised to see a dozen square-shaped objects with a central white light silently pass across the clear sky. The sighting lasted about a minute and a half. Only one other witness reported this sighting, on October 13, 2014. The observation of luminous objects crossing the sky in just a few minutes suggests Thai lanterns, likely licked nearby after a private party. The unusual shape described by the witness (square, with a central point of light and two wings) could be an interpretation of the barrel shape of classic Thai lanterns, or it could be the actual shape of a particular type of lantern. The movement is observed from west to east, which is consistent with the northwest wind recorded in the Nice weather forecast. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B," a probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of red lights.
description: Sunday, November 22, 2009, around 7:00 PM: observation of 7 to 8 red lights following one another in the same direction and without noise. The witness does not wish to give a statement to the police. She provided a photograph which is not very usable but resembles other photographs of sky lantern sightings.

summary: Observation of the slow passage OE of a bright point in the sky: observation of the passage of the international space station.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This particular observation was classified as eB in 2011 by GEIPAN. On December 17, 2009, GEIPAN received a direct testimony from an individual reporting the observation of a light moving from west to east on November 19, 2009, at 5:30 PM. The UFO was silent, and the observation lasted approximately three minutes. This case is part of a wave of local sightings. By comparing it with other cases, GEIPAN initially concluded that it was likely an observation of a disco projector. However, the described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color, trajectory) with a well-known spacecraft: the ISS (International Space Station). Furthermore, the ISS was indeed present in the observed area of the sky, even though the witness made no mention of it. Finally, the description provided by the witness from Buironfosse matches another observation recorded at the same time, which was clearly identified as an ISS pass. It is not the witness's visual perception that is at issue, but rather their interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (surprise, fatigue). In GEIPAN's current classification, this case of a weak anomaly is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misidentification of the ISS.

summary: Observations of the ISS pass.
description: On November 19, 2009, at approximately 5:35 PM, several people observed an object passing overhead that intrigued them. A bright white light moved slowly along a straight path. The observation lasted between 4 and 10 minutes, according to witnesses. These individuals, along with other witnesses, observed the passage of the ISS. A video was recorded by another witness: (Geipan.mp4).

summary: Long observation of a yellow cylindrical light very close to the horizon, stationary then moving slowly: lack of information.
description: On November 19th, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon from their home for 10 minutes, which they could not explain. The light, cylindrical in shape, was a very bright yellow, and the UFO was initially stationary before slowly moving along a straight trajectory near the horizon. Of low strangeness and moderate consistency (single witness testimony, uncertain date, but very precise documentation provided), this case unfortunately cannot be identified due to the excessively long interval between the observation and the publication of the testimony, making any on-site investigation impossible. The hypothesis of mistaking the object for a headlight or spotlight mounted on some vehicle (presumably a land vehicle) cannot unfortunately be formally validated (see the investigation report). This case is classified as Class C due to the excessively long interval between the date of observation and the submission of the testimony (nearly four years). Furthermore, the date of the observation is uncertain.

summary: Observation of luminous phenomena.
description: On November 18, 2009, between 8:00 PM and 11:00 PM, a witness observed approximately ten objects with flashing lights. The observation lasted between 20 and 30 minutes. The entire group moved silently. The witness did not respond to GEIPAN's requests for additional information necessary for the investigation. The case is classified as C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the movement of an orange light in the sky.
description: witness reported an observation made on Wednesday, November 18, 2009, at 7:01 a.m. They saw an orange light moving. Its speed varied, with accelerations and decelerations along an irregular trajectory. The description of a faint orange light moving in a zigzag pattern at a low altitude, with changes in direction and speed seemingly influenced by the wind, strongly suggests the observation of a Thai-type sky lantern. The case is classified as Class B: probable observation of a sky lantern.

summary: Late report of a witness's observation of a red light moving across the night sky with a change of trajectory; end of observation reported indirectly: lack of information.
description: The testimony was given a year after the sighting and was triggered by a television program. On November 16, 2009, at approximately 7:45 PM, while driving towards Villefranche-sur-Mer (06), two people observed a bright red light moving across the night sky. The UFO changed trajectory and was then lost from sight by the witness. The witness had time to take a photograph and call a relative living in the direction the UFO disappeared. The witness reported that his relatives saw a reddish object land on the lower slopes of Mont Boron hill, then rise and quickly disappear in a white flash. Only one witness statement was collected. The trajectory perceived by the witness was that the UFO arrived from the east (Monaco), then, directly over his observation point (Villefranche-sur-Mer), it changed trajectory towards Nice. The change is actually quite small, on the order of 30 degrees, to take a southwesterly component (towards Nice) from an arrival from the east, and is associated with a perception of a descent (a steep, dipping wind) towards Nice. It is noted that the witness initially thought of a Thai lantern (a kind of bright red light very similar to a Thai lantern) but then seems to reject this hypothesis mainly due to the speed. However, the measured wind is consistent with the trajectory. Closest to the observation point (3 km from Saint-Jean-Cap-Ferrat), the wind is blowing towards the southwest. At Nice airport (9 km), this wind is shifting at that time, moving from southwest to southeast, which indicates that in such a mountainous and coastal environment, the wind can be highly variable from one point and moment to the next, probably also with horizontal gusts and sudden dips. The wind was not weak, 10 km/h with gusts up to 30 km/h. The perceived strangeness in terms of speed could result from the inability to accurately judge the distance. The photograph reveals nothing that would either validate or invalidate the lantern hypothesis. The subsequent observation no longer comes from the witness but from his mother, and is reported by the witness. What the mother initially saw is consistent with the lantern hypothesis, as she saw a reddish object land on the hills. The color is no longer the blazing red seen by the main witness, but a reddish hue consistent with the lantern's fading phase. It should be noted that the highly variable wind could also have blown the lantern back towards the hill while it was still brightly lit. However, the final phase is no longer consistent: the slow rise could still be plausible if the lantern was still lit and managed to rise after being pushed to the ground by the wind, but not the final disappearance in a white flash in less than a second. It is unknown whether the mother continuously observed the UFO (she called her son to tell him about its end) or if she may have confused it with another similar phenomenon. Up to this last point, the observation is consistent with a Thai lantern flight. The strangeness of this observation (compared to a Thai hypothesis, which would otherwise be accepted) lies solely in elements that were not directly reported to GEIPAN, despite GEIPAN's request for testimony from the mother via the witness. The testimony is therefore inconsistent. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies it as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Successive observations of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On November 14th and 15th, 2009, witnesses reported seeing a blue light moving across the sky. The first sighting on November 14th received media attention, and other people reported similar sightings in towns further north, such as Buironfosse (02) and Beaurieux (59). Witnesses described a round blue light in the sky, moving slowly from right to left (although they disagreed on the distance and origin of the phenomenon). A third sighting on November 21st was identified by the police as a spotlight from one of the local nightclubs. This plausible hypothesis likely explains the sightings of November 14th and 15th, 2009.

summary: Observation of unusual movements of a bluish light beam: probable laser animation.
description: On Sunday, November 15, 2009, around 9:00 PM, two people out for a walk were intrigued by the unusual movements of a bluish beam of light coming from the sky. The beam swept across the sky, undulating and oscillating, giving the impression of following the couple. The phenomenon lasted 35 minutes, and no sound came from the beam. This case is similar to that of Jeantes (02) on November 14, 2009, which also reported an observation on November 15 at 8:55 PM. The Hirson Gendarmerie identified the observed phenomenon as a disco spotlight. Since the time of the two observations coincides, and the region has several possible locations for this type of spotlight, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": very probable confusion with a disco spotlight.

summary: Probable sighting of a military balloon equipped with powerful lighting.
description: On November 12, 2009, a witness noticed that a room in their home was lit up and that the light appeared to be coming from an oval-shaped object floating in the air, aligned with a line of utility poles. The observation lasted 20 seconds, and no noise was heard. No other witnesses reported the incident. Further investigation by the IPN (National Police Institute) revealed work carried out in November 2009 on the EDF (French Electricity Board) pylon in the direction of the observation and the presence nearby of a military balloon with a powerful light. These findings provided a rational explanation for the observation, allowing the investigation to be concluded and the case closed. This case, which initially seemed somewhat unusual, is likely explained by the observation of a military balloon, which was powerfully illuminated at the time of the observation.

summary: Observation of a flying lantern passing by.
description: Upon closing his shutters at 6:15 PM, a witness observed a large orange and yellow light coming from the southeast. During the one-minute observation, no sound was heard. This light then moved north and disappeared from his sight. Following a police investigation, the witness formally identified the photograph of the unidentified flying object (UFO) as a luminous balloon of the Thai lantern type.

summary: Observation of a circular light in the clouds.
description: On November 10, 2009, at approximately 8:30 PM, a witness observed a large, circular light in the clouds. An aircraft appeared to veer off course to avoid the light, which then suddenly disappeared. The witness declined to provide further information by reporting the incident to the police. The aircraft's flight path was clearly following a normal flight path (near the airport). No further reports were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack sufficient information.

summary: observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On November 9, 2009, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon passing between two mountains at a distance of approximately 800 meters, lasting less than a minute. Red in color and round in shape, followed by flames, this object moved northward toward Tontouta. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon, which resembled an atmospheric reentry, but about which we lack information.

summary: Observation of teches in photographs.
description: One day in November 2009 (the witness did not give the exact date and time), while taking a virtual tour on Google Maps, a witness observed about ten light-colored "teches" as well as one darker one. These "teches" are photographic artifacts, that is to say, defects that appear in the photo, and whose causes can be varied (teches, dust, reflections).

summary: Observations of the ballet of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of an animation by laser beams.
description: On October 31, 2009, around 3:30 a.m., a witness observed a display of several luminous orbs in the sky, repeatedly colliding with each other. He eventually woke his partner, who witnessed the same phenomenon. This continued for several hours. The witness finally went back to bed around 5:00 a.m., while the phenomenon was still unfolding. The phenomenon observed on the night of October 31, 2009, in Le Raincy (93), was probably due to the rotation of two sky trackers (see investigation report). The location of the display could not be found and confirmed. This case of observation, classified as low strangeness, is categorized as B: probable observation of a light display caused by laser beams.

summary: Probable observations of natural phenomena.
description: witness has reported their filmed observations. These are two sightings (October 27, 2009, and November 13, 2009) made by the same witness from the same location. Both observations describe white streaks in the sky (aircraft contrails and/or atmospheric trails) and the sighting of "black balls" crossing the sky at high speed (flocks of birds or insects in the foreground of the video sent by the witness to GEIPAN). In the absence of a police report and other investigative evidence, these two cases are classified as Category B, indicating probable observations of entirely natural phenomena.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of several dozen points of light.
description: On the afternoon of October 18th, a witness observed several dozen white lights high in the sky. They were moving very slowly from east to west. No other accounts were collected regarding this phenomenon, about which we lack information, even though it resembles a characteristic sighting of Thai lanterns.

summary: Atmospheric reentry of the Centaur stage of the Atlas rocket.
description: GEIPAN received numerous reports of observations made on Sunday, October 18, 2009, around 9:15 PM (local time) concerning the south-northwest passage of two bright points in the sky. These observations were made across the entire country. They very often describe one or two bright points of light followed by a white halo (like a comet's trail). No sound was heard. These observations correspond to the fuel release phase of the Centaur stage of an American military weather satellite, DSMP F18, launched by an Atlas rocket from Vanderberg Air Force Base in California (USA). This case is featured on the GEIPAN website. New reports are added regularly.

summary: Probable sighting of flying lanterns.
description: On October 17, 2009, at 11:30 PM, a witness filmed approximately ten flying objects 30 meters above the ground. During the 15-minute observation, the objects moved silently and in a coordinated manner toward the south-southwest. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected in the area. This witness likely observed the passage of sky lanterns.

summary: Observations by two witnesses of the movement of a gigantic shape with a sparkling ball: lack of information.
description: Two witnesses reported an observation made on October 14, 2009, around 9:00 PM: looking south, the primary witness saw a large, gray shape in the starry sky moving silently northward. Inside the shape, a sparkling sphere was observed. The second witness confirmed the presence of a large white circle with the consistency of smoke. No other reports were collected. The witnesses' descriptions were too vague to formulate a hypothesis. The case is classified as C.

summary: Probable observation of the movement of a land vehicle.
description: farmer observed, from a considerable distance, an object the size of a semi-trailer truck with numerous lights passing by. No noise was heard during the observation. The witness was not wearing his glasses at the time. Nevertheless, his initial impression was that of a combine harvester traveling with its work lights on (very likely in an agricultural area). His vision without glasses did not allow him to see the vehicle in detail as it traveled on the road. The estimated speed of 80 km/h seems obviously too high for a combine harvester, but not abnormal for a large convoy transporting this type of vehicle. The absence of noise can be explained by the wind direction (see weather conditions), which carried the sound in the opposite direction from the witness. This case is classified as Class B, as the highly probable observation of a large land vehicle traveling on the road.

summary: Probable sighting of flying lanterns.
description: On October 3, 2009, at approximately 9:30 PM, a family (witnesses 1 and 2) observed groups of bright, flying objects passing overhead. These round objects moved horizontally and rapidly. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted between six and seven minutes. The glow of these objects diminished before disappearing completely. The police investigation determined that they were Chinese lanterns released during a birthday celebration. The person responsible for the release (witness 3) provided some photographs taken at the event. The description of the observation by witnesses 1 and 2 at approximately 9:30 PM corresponds to the likely sighting of Thai lanterns. The launch of sky lanterns reported to the police (around 11:00 PM) by witness 3 does not correspond to the time of the observation. However, the data contained in the photos sent by witness 3 confirms this launch time of around 23:00.

summary: Observation of the silent N-NE passage of a luminous phenomenon in the shape of a water droplet: probable observation of a bolide.
description: On September 29, 2009, at 8:27 a.m., a witness in their garden observed a silent north-northeast passage of a bright white, teardrop-shaped object radiating a slightly bluish light for 30 to 50 seconds. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The low degree of strangeness of the observed phenomenon and the inconsistency of the witness's account do not allow for a definitive conclusion regarding a fireball, although the drawing made by the witness is typical of one. This case is classified as B: probable observation of a fireball.

summary: Laser beam used in meteorological research by the Faculty of Sciences of Saint-Denis.
description: Two witnesses reported seeing a green, flowering light rising vertically in the sky on several evenings between 10 p.m. and midnight. A police officer confirmed seeing this luminosity in the sky at the same times. The police investigation revealed that the atmospheric and cyclone studies laboratory at the Faculty of Sciences in Saint-Denis regularly uses a laser to study meteorological phenomena at night. The description of the stationary, flowering green light corresponds perfectly with the witnesses' accounts.

summary: Observation of the movement of slightly orange points forming a triangle: lack of information.
description: On September 27, 2009, at approximately 11:05 PM, a witness observed three slightly orange lights forming a triangle in the sky for two minutes. One of the lights split in two, and the witness then observed two separate phenomena. The entire system disappeared silently in the direction of the Saint-Germain-en-Laye forest. The testimony was too brief for an investigation to be conducted: the witness, contacted 18 months after the observation, declined to provide further information. This case is classified as Category C: Lack of Information.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On September 27, 2009, a witness reported via email seeing a peculiar luminous phenomenon at 2:25 a.m. Through a partially open shutter, he observed lights above his house. No noise was heard during the observation. These lights, initially red and then green, quickly disappeared. As the witness declined to provide further details, it is impossible to investigate further. The case is therefore classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a silver ball in the sky and instantaneous disappearance: probable sighting of a balloon.
description: On September 26, 2009, at 11:11 AM, a witness observed a very bright, silvery ball moving very slowly horizontally in the sky. It disappeared instantly. This observation was likely that of a balloon illuminated by the sun. Since there was no wind, it could have been a child's or fairground balloon that was relatively close and suddenly burst, or a weather balloon that was far away and high in the sky. This case is classified as Class B, like the probable observation of a balloon illuminated by the sun.

summary: Prolonged observation of an object flying in the sky that appeared to be rotating on itself: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN was contacted by a witness regarding a strange object observed in the sky over Thénes (74) during the Saint-Maurice agricultural fair on September 26, 2009. The object appeared to be rotating. The witness attached two photographs of the object to their email but did not complete a ground-based questionnaire or respond to requests for further details. They did not specify whether other witnesses had seen the phenomenon. This case is unusual only because of the object's shape: its movement appears to be that of a balloon, therefore an object "lighter than air." Unfortunately, the testimony is too inconsistent to allow for a firm conclusion, unless additional details about the observation are obtained. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of rapid movements and sudden stops of a white rectangular parallelepiped in the sky: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN was contacted by telephone on August 24, 2009, regarding an observation of several balls of light seen two days earlier (during the night of September 22-23, 2009). Contacted again a month later to obtain the Terrestrial Questionnaire related to this observation, the witness withdrew, having in the meantime discovered that they were Thai lanterns. He did, however, take the opportunity to report a strange phenomenon observed by his 7-year-old son on Thursday, September 24, 2009, around 7:00 PM. A questionnaire and a drawing were faxed to GEIPAN in October 2009. That evening, the child, playing in the garden, had his attention drawn to the sound of an airplane coming from the southwest. The child was then intrigued by a parallelepiped-shaped, opaque white object behind the airplane. The object tilted to pass under the aircraft, then plummeted to a stop below a high-voltage power line. It then moved towards the neighbor's TV antenna (10 meters high), climbed at high speed, stopped abruptly, and then moved vertically again, disappearing into the sky. During the observation, which lasted between 20 and 30 seconds, the sky was clear and cloudless. No other reports were filed with GEIPAN. A steady wind of 17 km/h was blowing from the north-northeast. The object, shaped like an opaque white parallelepiped, approached from the southwest of the observation site, i.e., into the wind. It plummeted to a stop at rooftop level, moved silently under the high-voltage power line, still against the wind, before moving vertically again and disappearing into the sky. No standard hypothesis can address these criteria. This case stems from the testimony of a 7-year-old child, an indirect testimony as it was reported by his father. GEIPAN did not deem it necessary to investigate further the testimony of a child of this age. Sincerity is not particularly in question, but a child of this age may be more easily influenced, even unconsciously, by discussions or situations in their immediate environment. This influence can lead to exaggerating or over-interpreting observed elements that may have been commonplace to begin with. It should be noted that the father had already given a first report to GEIPAN a month earlier. This other observation was quickly explained (Thai lanterns), but it may have created this factor of influence or anxiety in the child related to the possible strangeness of the sky. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Very brief observations of phenomena in the sky.
description: witness reports two observations. While on vacation in the Aude region around July 22, 2009, at approximately 11:00 PM (the witness no longer remembers the exact date), he observed a very bright, slightly oval sphere moving from west to east in the sky. Abruptly changing trajectory, the phenomenon disappeared into space. Possible hypotheses such as ball lightning or meteors could not be verified due to uncertainties regarding the exact date and time of the observation. A meteor shower occurred on July 25, 2009, around 11:45 PM local time, but this does not appear to correspond to the observation. On September 24, 2009, at 7:55 AM from his home, this witness observed a flying object moving north-south in the sky, which intrigued him. The object quickly disappeared. A likely hypothesis is that it was an airplane illuminated by the rising sun. These observation cases are classified as "C" due to a lack of precision and information.

summary: Observations of the movement of points of light in the sky.
description: On September 21, 2009, a motorist twice observed a yellow light moving across the sky. The questionnaire regarding this observation was only received by GEIPAN in February 2011. In the absence of a police report and preliminary investigation, it is impossible to draw conclusions from this single, rather vague testimony (the very brief phenomena, nighttime driving, observation through the window of the moving vehicle, and very low altitude above the road suggest the possibility of headlight or streetlight reflection). This testimony is inconsistent and does not present any unusual characteristics. The unexplained case is classified as C due to a lack of information and the impossibility of further investigation.

summary: Observation of a light with a change in trajectory.
description: GEIPAN received a brief report of a peculiar observation made on September 16, 2009. A single witness observed a luminous phenomenon rapidly passing northward, changing trajectory several times. The phenomenon disappeared in a northwesterly direction. Despite our repeated requests, no further information has been gathered on this phenomenon, making any investigation impossible.

summary: Observation of a material form at the end of a cloud: lack of information.
description: On September 16, 2009, at 4:26 a.m., a witness observed an unexplained phenomenon in the sky. He reported to the police that he had seen a material shape at the edge of a cloud. The object was round with three or four illuminated windows. Beneath this object, he also observed a bar topped with an ovoid light moving laterally from left to right. The phenomenon was stationary, at a low altitude, and was visible for more than five minutes. No other witness statements were collected regarding this phenomenon, and no further information was provided during the police investigation. Despite a request from GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Special Investigation Group), the witness did not provide any additional information, thus preventing any precise investigation. The case is classified as C due to lack of information.

summary: Observations of a dark mass with two flashing lights; slight humming and slow movement of the object: probable observation of a small airship, possibly remote controlled, probably electrically propelled.
description: On September 13, 2009, between 9:30 and 10:00 PM, two gendarmes on patrol observed a motionless, dark, stationary mass above the Chahaignes town hall. Elongated in shape, with two wing-like features and two asynchronously flashing red lights, the object then moved slowly. A faint humming sound was heard coming from it. Leaving the village, the patrol observed the mass again; it was at a very low altitude above the fields and appeared to be following the contours of the land. Continuing their patrol, the gendarmes left the object behind, and it had disappeared by the time they returned to the area. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. This observation is considered highly credible, thanks to two reliable witnesses and a very detailed report filed with the gendarmerie. The strangeness is moderate, as the observed object has many characteristics of a small civilian airship: size, shape, lighting, and flight dynamics. What makes this case so strange is that it was nighttime, the craft was flying very low, taking significant risks and violating regulations, and no trace of it was found in the region at sites where this type of craft is known. GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of a small airship, possibly remote-controlled, probably electrically powered.

summary: Observation of the movement with change of direction of an orange luminous ball: lack of information.
description: This unusual case exhibits characteristics of Thae lanterns: orange color, fiery appearance, and initial movement following a northeast wind (19 to 50 km/h). The observation report is very brief and does not mention the precise location or directions of observation. The observed erratic movement could possibly be explained by wind gusts, but this cannot be substantiated. This report is classified as "C": insufficient information to draw a conclusion; incomplete report; inability to model wind gusts in an urban environment.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of a bright, non-flickering light: probable ISS passage.
description: On September 8, 2009, at 9:14 PM, a witness observed a bright, non-flickering light in the sky moving rapidly from west to east along a straight trajectory. This testimony is not very unusual, and the description is too brief for a serious study. It is very likely a pass of the International Space Station (ISS) moving from west to east above the southern horizon between 9:07 PM and 9:14 PM (see Calsky's observation). GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": observation of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation of a bright ball with strong intermittent flashes.
description: On September 7, 2009, at approximately 6:10-6:15 PM, a witness observed a "bright ball with strong, intermittent flashes" in the west-northwest sky above Paris. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. As the witness declined to complete a standard observation questionnaire, any investigation is impossible due to a lack of precise information. The case is classified as "C".

summary: Observing the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On Sunday, September 6, 2009, two witnesses observed several orange orbs, all equidistant from each other, passing overhead from their homes. No sound was heard during the observation. Local media reported in the following days that numerous people had made a similar observation that night and that photos and videos had been taken. These sightings were attributed to the release of approximately one hundred Thai lanterns during a wedding celebration.

summary: Observation of luminous orbs passing in the sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On Sunday, September 6th, at 12:24 AM, a witness observed 12 luminous yellow-orange orbs moving silently across the sky from their terrace. They followed an upward trajectory, their light gradually fading. One of the photographs (DSC 03903) provided by the witness allowed for the identification of the Moon's position relative to the orbs, thus correcting the witness's initial observation direction, which proved to be incorrect. The orbs appeared to be floating in a southeasterly direction, consistent with prevailing winds. The phenomenon's duration (no more than 5 minutes), the gradual fading of the lights, the slow trajectory, the variation in the relative positions of the orbs, the timing of the observation (Saturday night/Sunday morning), and the yellow-orange color all support the hypothesis of Thai lanterns. Having failed to find the origin of these lanterns, GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Probable sighting of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: Between midnight and 12:15 a.m., a witness observed three luminous orange orbs moving silently and in a straight line from their windows. After changing direction, they disappeared, rising into the sky. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected. The witness's description perfectly matches that of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of an orange luminous object: probable observation of the movement of a Thai lantern.
description: During a street meal on September 5, 2009, around 10:00 PM, several people observed a luminous object silently passing across the sky. One witness reported seeing an orange ball moving slowly before suddenly speeding off southward, still without making a sound. The characteristics of the observation seem to indicate a well-known phenomenon frequently reported to GEIPAN: the passage of a luminous sky lantern. The presence of fireworks nearby, and therefore of festive activity, significantly strengthens this hypothesis. This case is classified as Class B, indicating the probable sighting of a luminous sky lantern.

summary: Probable sighting of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On September 5, 2009, at approximately 12:10 a.m., two witnesses at their home observed four intense, bright orange lights moving north-south. No sound was heard during the five-minute observation. They disappeared westward in an upward trajectory. The description perfectly matches that of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the passage of a flying object resembling a weather balloon: lack of information.
description: witness reported an observation made from a vehicle: while traveling between Nîmes and Russan in the Gard department, they saw a white object, resembling a hot air balloon or weather balloon, moving in the sky several times on Friday, September 4, 2009, between 8:00 and 8:30 a.m. Although the witness took a photograph, and despite our repeated requests, no further details will be provided, making any investigation impossible due to a lack of information.

summary: Presence of an object in a photograph without direct observation during the shooting: probable bird.
description: A witness sent us a photograph showing an object that the witness did not see when the photograph was taken. The witness did not provide a specific date (referring to a weekend in September 2009). Analyzing a photograph after the fact, without direct observation, is often complicated. The unidentified object in photo 100_0726 appears to be a bird, the dark underside of whose wings can be seen in the shadows.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous orange cylindrical shape: lack of information.
description: hunter observed a cylindrical orange object in the sky around 5:00 AM on August 31, 2009. Using binoculars, the witness described a uniform, bright, almost fluorescent color. Initially stationary, the object began to rise in a pendulum-like motion for about ten minutes. It then descended in the same manner before disappearing. The event took place over the English Channel, several kilometers from the coast. Several hypotheses were considered (flares, torch, boat, helicopter, airplane), but none were deemed suitable. This rather strange observation warranted a field investigation, but GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) was unable to contact the witness; moreover, more than three years after the event, verification would be risky. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of a pair of lights above the sea: lack of information.
description: witness reported an observation made at night on August 30 or 31, 2009, from the terrace of his home. A pair of flashing, stationary lights appeared above the sea. Using binoculars, the witness noted that these lights were connected by "a flat, elongated base, like a line." After twenty to thirty minutes of observation, the object finally moved away to the east. No other witness statements were collected. On an old photograph he sent us, the witness sketched his observation. The time given (approximately) 2:30 a.m. was not confirmed by the investigator (see investigation report). The hypotheses (scintillation of celestial bodies, stars, and even planets, as well as possible lights from ships or lights on Pianosa Island) are considered unlikely. This case of observation is actually quite unusual, but the weak consistency of the testimony and the impossibility of validating the hypothesis of fires at sea prevent a clear conclusion. This case is classified as Class C due to the inconsistencies identified.

summary: Observation of the successive arrival and movement of about ten red-orange luminous points in the night sky and rapid disappearance: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: This is an observation from 2009, reported three years later. The witness states, "A large majority of the people I reported these events to laughed at me. However, after careful consideration, I now believe that your official organization should take my observations and photos into account." During a festive evening on a terrace at 11:00 PM, a bright red-orange point followed by about ten other points were seen moving across the starry sky. The whole thing stopped for 30 seconds, then each point disappeared one by one. No sound was heard. Fifteen people observed the phenomenon. Only the witness provided a report accompanied by photographs. The observation has many characteristics of Thai lanterns, particularly the colors, the movement in formation, and the lights going out one by one. The photos provided also support this hypothesis. The movement and subsequent stop are consistent with the weather forecast, which indicated wind with small gusts. The sudden extinction of the flame is often interpreted as a departure at dizzying speed. This account clearly illustrates the emotion this interpretation can evoke; the witness clarifies, "It's simply a UFO, because current technology on Earth doesn't allow for such a speed of acceleration into space." By 2008, Thai lanterns were already on the market. It was a summer weekend evening, conducive to festive events. GEIPAN classified the case as category B: probable observation of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of several red-orange luminous phenomena in the sky: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.
description: On Friday, August 28, 2009, around 9:00 PM, a motorist observed several red-orange lights slowly moving across the sky. Other witnesses also watched the phenomenon. No further reports were collected. This observation is considered to have a low degree of strangeness. This case is classified as Class B: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.

summary: Probable sightings of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 25, 2009, around 11:00 PM, two walkers observed two stationary red-orange orbs just above the trees. During the five-minute observation, no sound was heard. A few minutes later, one of the witnesses, returning home, noticed that the orbs had disappeared. The characteristics of the two stationary, red-orange luminous orbs suggest the probable sighting of Thai lanterns. Another account published in the local press reported a similar sighting in Arzon the same evening: the trajectories given in both cases, as well as the descriptions, confirm the similarity between the different probable sightings of flying lanterns.

summary: Probable sightings of Thai lanterns passing by.
description: witness reported his observations on August 23rd and 24th, 2009, during which he observed the movement of red luminous phenomena in the sky. Other testimonies were collected. The witness's detailed description perfectly matches that of Thai lanterns. Even though the witness noted that their speed of movement was inconsistent with the wind that day, this rapid movement can be explained by very localized atmospheric movements: the atmosphere can be disturbed during summer nights by various causes, particularly thermal updrafts above certain buildings or fields.

summary: Observation of two metallic-colored objects.
description: witness observed two silvery-gray spheres moving rapidly and silently. The described characteristics of the observation correspond to those known for balloons (metallic-looking spheres moving silently, trajectories drifting with the wind away from the witness). The observation was made on a Sunday in the early afternoon (2:15 PM local time) in the direction of a densely populated urban area. The case is weak (single witness, brief and incomplete observation report). The hypothesis of balloons or other flying objects cannot be verified due to a lack of information and the weak evidence.

summary: Observations in the sky of the movement of four bright points creating different geometric shapes: lack of information.
description: On August 23, 2009, between 6:15 and 6:30 PM, people observed four bright points of light moving high in the sky. These points formed geometric shapes that intrigued the observers. Only one witness contacted GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimental and Astronomical Research). This testimony is actually quite unusual, and the description too brief for a serious study. It could simply have been four helium-filled balloons reflecting sunlight. The geometric shapes would then be merely the result of their movement due to the wind. However, GEIPAN has no concrete evidence to support this hypothesis. Unfortunately, this case was only investigated in 2012, too late to search for scientific or amateur balloon launches. Lacking precise data, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to insufficient information.

summary: Observation of a moving red dot.
description: walker in the Fontainebleau forest reported observing a bright red light at approximately 10:15 PM on August 22, 2009, 30 meters above the horizon. The witness then observed the object moving before it disappeared. The observation lasted about six minutes. The witness did not respond to the various letters sent to him and therefore did not provide enough information for GEIPAN to conduct an investigation. This case is classified as Class C due to lack of information.

summary: Observations of the silent passage of an orange ball in the sky: probable passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On August 22, 2009, at approximately 9:30 PM, several people observed the passage of a luminous orange sphere. It moved in a straight line from west to east; no sound was heard during the observation. The sphere stopped before disappearing at very high speed to the south. GEIPAN later received email reports from two other witnesses. The observation had the characteristics of Thai lanterns: orange color, movement consistent with the wind (light and variable, predominantly westerly), and a local festival nearby (Rencontres de Maubourguet). The object's apparent temporary immobility could be explained by its movement in front of the observers; the object's disappearance corresponds to the extinguishing of the flame. GEIPAN classified this case as 'B': probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the presence and then movement in the sky of an oval phenomenon with lights: lack of information.
description: On August 21, 2009, at 9:49 PM, a witness observed an oval-shaped object in the sky for three minutes. The object was equipped with a powerful white light and smaller lights. Initially stationary, it then moved in a straight line without any sound being heard. The witness's wife also observed the phenomenon and took photographs. This observation is accompanied by several photos provided by the witness. These photos, however, do not accurately represent the observation and are clearly the result of computer processing. Given this, the photos are considered unusable. The observation of the phenomenon itself remains somewhat strange due to its rectilinear movement, possibly explained by the observation of a low-flying aircraft. Based on the conclusions drawn from the photo analysis, GEIPAN classifies this case as C due to a lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of two yellow-orange balls.
description: On August 20, 2009, at 9:37 PM, a person observed two yellow-orange spheres moving from east to west without any sound being heard. The phenomenon quickly disappeared from the witness's field of vision. Despite several attempts to contact the witness for further information, no details were obtained regarding this observation. Any investigation was therefore impossible.

summary: Observation of a fireball passing by.
description: On August 18, 2009, a person observed a luminous phenomenon from their terrace. During the observation, which lasted approximately seven seconds, the witness saw a yellow-orange sphere followed by a trail moving from northwest to south. The phenomenon gradually disappeared on a downward trajectory. Although the brief description of the observation suggests a possible atmospheric reentry, an investigation could not be conducted due to a lack of information, despite our repeated requests.

summary: Probable sighting of Thai lanterns.
description: On August 16, 2009, at approximately 10:30 PM, two walkers observed two particularly bright, stationary objects in the sky for four minutes. These objects then moved silently as their brightness decreased. They eventually disappeared, obscured by mist. The description given by one of the witnesses and the photographs taken clearly suggest a possible sighting of sky lanterns.

summary: Observation of the EO passage of a brown ovoid object. Straight trajectory.
description: witness reported an observation that took place on August 15, 2009, at 1:15 PM from his garden. He saw a matte brown, ovoid shape pass in the sky along a straight trajectory. The phenomenon moved from east to west in the direction of Cognac. No noise was heard during the observation. No other witness accounts of this phenomenon have been reported. The hypothesis of a passing airplane or helicopter was ruled out by the witness and could not be verified with air traffic control due to the late receipt of the police report by GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group). Several other hypotheses were considered for this unusual case, including the possibility of very close objects such as a rugby ball, a clay pigeon, a frisbee, or a model aircraft, but these do not correspond to the witness's account (the phenomenon clearly passed over the rooftops). The hypothesis of an atmospheric reentry of a meteorite was also considered (period of high meteoritic activity, peak of the Perseid meteor shower) but impossible to verify without further evidence. In the absence of a solid hypothesis, this case is classified as D1: a moderately consistent unexplained case (only one witness) with a marked strangeness.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: lack of information to validate hypotheses.
description: On August 15, 2009, between 11:15 PM and 11:25 PM, a pedestrian on the promenade in Menton observed a stationary luminous phenomenon in the sky to the right of the North Star. After three minutes of observation, the intensity of the light decreased. The phenomenon then rapidly ascended vertically and disappeared in two seconds in the direction of Italy. This occurred over the Mediterranean Sea. Several hypotheses were analyzed (flare, pyrotechnic balloon, airplane, satellite) and remain possible, but could not be confirmed (see investigation report). This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information to fully confirm or refute any of these hypotheses.

summary: Probable sighting of a flight of Thai lanterns.
description: On the night of August 15-16, 2009, people observed orange orbs in the sky. A video was recorded. The video, available on YouTube, shows a very likely flight of Thai lanterns.

summary: Atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.
description: On August 15, 2009, at 10:00 PM, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon moving for approximately 40 seconds. It was luminescent green and elongated in shape. No sound was heard. The witness observed the atmospheric reentry of a meteorite: the green color comes from ionization in the upper atmosphere. This meteorite was observed from Bele in Switzerland to the far south of Great Britain.

summary: Observation of the silent and rapid SO-NE passage of an orange-colored object: lack of information.
description: On August 14, 2009, at approximately 10:55 PM, a witness was intrigued by the rapid SE/NW passage of a round, reddish-orange object across the sky. No trail was observed during the 2 to 3 seconds of observation. At 11:10 PM, the witness made a second, one-second observation of another object passing SE/NW. This case suggests the observation of a bolide (meteorite fall), but the absence of a trail is surprising, and GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimental and Observatory of Astronomical Phenomena) has not found any confirmation from other observations. Of moderate strangeness due to its linear movement, this observation suffers from excessive imprecision and therefore lacks sufficient evidence at this stage. A field investigation would likely yield little information more than four years after the event. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of independent witness statements and corroborating evidence.

summary: Filmed observation from an airplane of the appearance of a dark spot.
description: Shortly after takeoff, a passenger observed a dark, stationary object that suddenly disappeared. A few minutes later, another object of the same type appeared. The witness recorded two videos of his observations. Unfortunately, the poor-quality videos, which may have shown a balloon at low altitude just after takeoff, are unusable, making any investigation or verification impossible.

summary: Brief observation in the sky of an oval-shaped, light grey object by a motorist: lack of information.
description: On August 12, 2009, at approximately 5:05 PM, a motorist briefly observed a light gray, silvery, slightly shiny, oval-shaped object ahead of him, at an altitude of 20 degrees above a hill. The object disappeared very quickly behind the hill. No other witness accounts were collected. This observation, remarkably well described and contextualized by the witness's experience with astronomical observations, is consistent but unfortunately too brief to properly assess its strangeness. Hypotheses involving balloons or aircraft are conceivable, but not verifiable with the available information. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of data on the object, independent witness statements, and corroborating evidence.

summary: Probable sighting of bright flying lanterns.
description: On August 12, 2009, at approximately 11:10 PM, a witness in his garden observed the supernova passage of two ovoid-shaped objects following one another. Orange in color, they were located quite high in the sky and moved along a straight trajectory. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted 30 seconds. The sole witness, who spontaneously gave his statement to the police, appeared to be familiar with the visual characteristics of shooting stars, which he had hoped to observe, as well as those of aircraft traffic related to the proximity of Lyon-Saint Exupéry Airport. Both of these hypotheses can be ruled out. The characteristics of the 30-second observation described by the witness (two slightly dim, oval, pale orange lights following each other, flying at a low altitude along a straight trajectory, one of the lights oscillating, and no noise) suggest the possibility of Thai-type sky lanterns. The absence of a steady wind does not contradict the likelihood of the lanterns being released from the south of the observation site (the area around the municipal stadium). The single witness statement provides little support for this observation. The level of strangeness is low, and a large proportion of the described characteristics correspond to those of a flight of sky lanterns. This case is classified as Class B, indicating a probable sighting of sky lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent evolutions of a luminous sphere above the sea: light animation linked to an advertising campaign.
description: On August 11, 2009, between 4:45 and 5:20 a.m., two people observed a bright white point of light with a greenish outline above the sea. No sound was heard during the object's variable speed and its rapid departure out to sea. The witnesses noted that two pleasure boats were in the vicinity of the phenomenon. The sighting in Canet-en-Roussillon occurred during a nighttime advertising campaign conducted by the Buzzman agency for the SyFy channel on the night of August 10-11, 2009, between Canet and Argelès (see the investigation report). The theme, "Close Encounters of the Third Kind," and the special effects used for this campaign are consistent with the unusual observation made by the two witnesses. The very early hour of this animation (4:45 am) corresponds to the end of the animation that began the evening before in the neighboring town of Argeles. This case is perfectly explained and therefore classified as an A-rated light show for an advertising campaign.

summary: Observation of a disc-shaped, silvery-white object above a wind turbine.
description: On August 8, 2009, around 11:00-11:30 PM, a driver observed a disc-shaped but slightly oval, silvery object above a wind turbine for two or three seconds. Her passenger did not have time to see the phenomenon, as it disappeared very quickly. This case, submitted late to the analysis of the panel of experts working with GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information on Unidentified Aerial Phenomena), was subjected to an inconclusive preliminary investigation by the IPN (National Police). The strong emotional state of the main witness should be noted. The analysis shows that the size of the observed UFO (Unidentified Aerial Phenomenon) corresponds to the possible size of the Moon's reflection on the wind turbine blade (a reflection mentioned by the main witness). Apart from this plausible hypothesis, the observation presents a low degree of strangeness and was observed by only one witness from inside a car. The second witness did not make a direct observation. The case is classified "C" as an unexplained case with little consistency and no unusual characteristics.

summary: Probable observation of the movement of Thai lanterns.
description: On the night of August 7, 2009, around 1:00 AM, several people observed two luminous phenomena composed of two reddish, spherical shapes. These moved silently. Only one witness out of about ten observers gave a statement. The description of the parallel trajectories of the two luminous phenomena, moving slowly and seemingly hovering, with one slowly fading away, suggests the probable passage of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the movement of an orange ball: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: witness reported an observation made on August 7, 2009, at 9:20 PM in Golf-Juan, a seaside resort in the commune of Vallauris (06): his son observed the movement and change of direction of an intriguing orange, spherical object in the sky. The main witness went out onto the first-floor balcony and indeed observed the silent, constant-speed movement of an orange sphere at a high altitude. A photograph was taken. The object moved away, then faded, turning gray before disappearing completely, hidden by a hill. The description of the flying object corresponds to that of a Thai lantern: the speed of movement is consistent with local weather conditions (little wind, variable thermal breezes), as is the duration of the observation (3 minutes), and the description of the object's disappearance. The witness interpreted this object as distant and very large, a common misconception since it is impossible to estimate the distance of an unknown object. Geipan classifies this case as "B": probable passage of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous sphere.
description: On August 7, 2009, between 11:10 PM and 11:15 PM, two witnesses observed the silent passage of a very bright sphere. It moved slowly along a north-south axis. Despite several attempts to contact the witnesses, too little information was gathered. This case is classified as Class C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of a point of light.
description: On August 6, 2009, at approximately 4:25 a.m., a witness briefly observed a fixed point of light (3 seconds) in the sky east of Polaris. It gradually faded away. The witness provided no further information about this phenomenon.

summary: Probable observation of Jupiter.
description: On the night of August 5, 2009, around 2:00 AM, two people observed a particularly bright circular object from their home. While filming the phenomenon, the main witness noticed a very slow horizontal movement of the object. Astronomical configurations and an appeal for witnesses confirmed that the observation was made on a full moon. The "phenomenon" was to the left of the full moon. The astronomical configuration indicated a very probable observation of the planet Jupiter, particularly visible at this time of year (apparent magnitude -2.8 with its maximum angular diameter of 48 arcseconds).

summary: Unusual movements of a round, white, luminous shape in the sky. No flashing or noise: lack of information.
description: Recent report (November 26, 2011) of an old observation, the exact date of which is unknown (August 25 or 26, 2009, according to the email of May 26, 2011). A witness reported observing unusual movements of a round, white, luminous shape in the sky. No flashing or noise was noted. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon. The following hypotheses were considered: a helicopter scanning the observation area, or a piece of construction equipment in the nearby quarry (Carrière de la Fosse), located northwest of the observation point. The lack of a precise date, the relatively early date of the observation, and its limited unusual nature preclude launching an investigation. The case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information, pending any additional evidence.

summary: Observation of the movement of a dark mass.
description: witness reported by telephone that on July 31, 2009, at approximately 8:47 PM, he observed a dark mass, larger than a star, passing from south to north. He stated that he took several photographs during the observation, which lasted eight minutes. Unfortunately, no further information was gathered, making any investigation impossible.

summary: Observation of the movement of a white luminous point with change of direction and acceleration.
description: On July 26, 2009, at approximately 10:20 PM, a witness, sitting on his terrace, was observing the starry sky. For 7 to 8 seconds, he followed the linear movement of a white light at an elevation of 25° to 35°, which he interpreted as the movement of a satellite. After looking away from this light for one to two seconds, the witness was surprised not to see it again along its trajectory. However, he then spotted another light beginning a westward turn for 2 to 3 seconds (in the direction of Habsheim airfield). This light then followed a high-speed linear trajectory, passing directly overhead. No unusual noise was heard during the observation, which lasted 10 to 12 seconds and ended at 11:48 PM. The witness remained intrigued by the overall trajectory of the light, including a change of direction and a significant acceleration of the phenomenon, all without any sound being heard. Even though there is no way to definitively state that it was the trajectory of a single point of light, several hypotheses have been ruled out: aircraft flyovers (no radar trace in the Rixsheim area between 11:30 PM and midnight), the presence of celestial bodies (Jupiter was too low on the horizon), and the passage of a satellite (Cosmos 1151-Rocket, but at an elevation of 57°). The phenomenon, while not particularly unusual, remains unexplained. The D1 classification is justified by the single witness report and the impossibility of estimating the distance of the phenomenon.

summary: Probable observation of the movement of a ball.
description: On July 25, 2009, around 7:00 PM, several witnesses observed a white flying object. One of the intrigued witnesses described a white sphere moving silently across the valley from north to south at a constant speed and altitude. The object suddenly gained altitude, accelerating, and then immediately disappeared into the sky. The slow, silent movement of the white sphere, its size, its trajectory across the valley, and the subsequent acceleration, likely due to wind resistance, suggest the probable observation of a balloon (of the weather balloon type, as described by the witness).

summary: Filmed observation of Thai lanterns.
description: The video associated with the observation leaves no doubt about the origin of the phenomenon: flying lanterns (also known as Thai lanterns).

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a very bright ball at approximately 2.50 m above the ground: observation of ball lightning.
description: Recent report (July 7, 2013) of an earlier case from July 23, 2009. At 11:00 PM on July 23, 2009, a person lying on a deck chair watching shooting stars was startled by the appearance of a very bright ball behind a shed. It moved silently, rising and falling alternately at about 2.5 meters above the ground. The ball then passed over the witness, who was still lying in the deck chair. The ball, white and yellow in color, was about the size of a child's ball. The phenomenon disappeared behind some trees. The phenomenon shone like the sun, emitting beams of light. The witness's description evoked ball lightning. The witness did not mention a storm, but it was hot, and there had been a thunderstorm that morning. The testimony was submitted to a lightning specialist (Lightning Laboratory: lightning laboratory) who unequivocally recognized a ball lightning phenomenon; numerous lightning strikes were recorded in Aquitaine that evening, reinforcing this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": observation of ball lightning.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of four pale yellow lights: probable observation of Thai lanterns.
description: On Wednesday, July 22nd, at 12:45 AM, a witness observed four pale yellow lights moving towards Paris from his home. He went to get his camera and upon returning, only one light remained, which he photographed before it too disappeared. The description matches observations of flying lanterns (known as Thai lanterns), and the wind direction recorded in Paris at the time of the observation reinforces this hypothesis. This case of observation, of low strangeness and moderate consistency given the limited details in the questionnaire and the few discrepancies between it and the information provided by telephone, most likely boils down to a case of mistaken identity with Thai lanterns. This case is classified as Class B: probable observation of the passage of Thai lanterns.

summary: Observation of the silent movement OE of a white luminous point: ISS passage
description: On July 21, 2009, two people observed a white light moving silently from west to east in the sky before disappearing over the horizon. One of the witnesses took photographs and contacted GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) by telephone to report his observation. He then sent his direct testimony along with the attached photos. This case is classified as "A": The witness observed the passage of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation of the movement of four lights: probably Thai lanterns.
description: On July 21, 2009, at approximately 12:40 a.m., a witness observed four red lights passing in the north-south sky from their home. No noise was heard during the observation, which lasted about two minutes. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. The information provided suggests a possible passage of Thai lanterns. There are no photos or videos, but the description—once again describing red-orange lights, a silent movement, a low altitude, a sudden disappearance—and the increasing number of observations of this type of phenomenon lead to the classification of this case as likely identified.

summary: Long observation of a silent, oblong-shaped object stationary above the houses: unusable testimony.
description: Unexplained cases hold potential for scientific knowledge, provided that their unexplained nature remains valid over time. Therefore, these cases are revisited. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over recent years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D1 and formerly named GIVET (08) 20.07.2009, is part of a set of cases recently re-examined. On July 20, 2009, around noon, a person gardening suddenly noticed a bright, cigar-shaped object with a small fin. The object was silent and remained stationary above the houses in their neighborhood. The front of the object was pointing towards the northeast, but the rest of the object was difficult to distinguish. The witness described "a sort of commotion" above the object. The observation lasted about ten minutes, after which the frightened witness returned home. No other witness statements were collected regarding this phenomenon. No theft incidents were reported to the police. The observation is very strange, both because of the elements described and the angular size (20 meters wide at a distance of 10 meters) of the object as described (see the investigation report). Confirmation of the second point during a second meeting with the witness rules out any explanatory hypothesis and makes the observation even stranger. Indeed, the angular size combined with the angular position (which was not vertical but within sight without looking up) makes it inconceivable that this UFO would not have been noticed (and reported) by the neighborhood in broad daylight (at midday) in an urban area (a neighborhood survey was conducted). The consistency of the testimony is insufficient to validate the unexplained or inexplicable nature of this sighting. This would have required several independent witnesses or evidence such as photographs or other traces. Here, the single witness raises questions due to his behavior in the face of such an unusual event; in particular, he stopped observing the sighting to go eat while the UFO was still present, 10 meters away and 20 meters wide, and despite having a camera. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: unusable testimony.

summary: Probable successive sightings of flying lanterns.
description: Between July 19th and 21st, 2009, a witness observed intriguing luminous phenomena from their home for a few seconds. Luminous spheres appeared at night between 10:50 PM and 11:15 PM. No sound was heard as the objects moved in a straight line before quickly fading and disappearing. The witness sent us photomontages of their successive observations. The described characteristics (multiple lights, straight trajectory) are consistent with the likely observation of sky lanterns. Sky lantern releases, which have become very popular recently, were the subject of a news item on our website.

summary: Observation of the ISS passing overhead.
description: On July 19, 2009, between 11:00 PM and 11:15 PM, a witness observed a very bright white light moving across the sky from northwest to southeast. No noise was heard during the slow movement of the object. The witness observed no smoke or traces on the ground. This person witnessed the passage of the International Space Station (ISS), which appeared particularly bright (magnitude -3.3).

summary: Observation of a stationary bright orange-red shape in the sky: lack of information.
description: On July 19, 2009, at approximately 10:40 PM, several people observed a silent, bright, reddish-orange shape in the sky. Despite some perceptible oscillations, the object remained stationary. Their observation lasted about 15 minutes; the object was then obscured by clouds. Only one eyewitness account has been reported. A tethered balloon illuminated by lights or spotlights from the ground (an advertising or festive balloon) could have given the same impression. A weather balloon at altitude, still illuminated by the sun an hour after sunset, could also have produced this appearance. It is very difficult to verify any of these hypotheses three years after the observation. The relative strangeness of this sighting stems solely from the static position of the observed phenomenon, and the single eyewitness account, despite a precise description, does not allow us to assess its consistency.
