Although balloon hypotheses are plausible, this case is class C due to a lack of independent testimony and cross-checking to validate a hypothesis.

summary: Possible sighting of flying lanterns.
description: On July 18, 2009, at approximately 10:40 PM, a witness observed about twenty luminous orange orbs above the horizon, moving horizontally and together. No sound was heard. The orbs disappeared from the witness's view due to the surrounding landscape. The characteristics of the described observation—about twenty non-dazzling luminous orbs moving slowly and simultaneously—strongly support the observation of a sky lantern formation.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of a white luminous phenomenon in the sky: passage of the ISS.
description: On July 17, 2009, at approximately midnight, a couple was intrigued by the rapid passage of a bright white phenomenon overhead. One of the witnesses reported observing it for 30 seconds. The phenomenon moved at a steady speed along a straight trajectory before disappearing. No unusual noises were noted during the observation. This case of observation, while not particularly unusual, is precisely described and corresponds in every respect to an observation of the International Space Station (ISS) passing overhead. This case is classified as Class A.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of reflections of light animation.
description: On July 15, 2009, between 12:26 and 12:28 AM, a witness observed and photographed a very bright luminous phenomenon in the cloudy sky from a fourth-floor balcony. No other witness statements were collected regarding this phenomenon. The investigator noted an inconsistency in the witness's account of the event's time: the witness wrote "from 12:26 to 12:28 AM" as a note and as indicated on the photos, whereas the photos themselves show 11:28 PM. The observation would therefore have taken place on July 14, 2009. If the time the photographs were taken was 11:28 PM, this coincides precisely with the time of the grand fireworks display launched from the Eiffel Tower to celebrate its 120th anniversary. The two-minute duration of the observation could correspond to the final burst of fireworks (see the link provided in the investigation report). If it was indeed 0:26, we can consider another light display, but one that is undetermined. This case is class B: probable observation of the reflection on the clouds of the light displays of July 14, 2009. The uncertainty in the time of observation makes it impossible to confirm whether it was the fireworks or another light display.

summary: Observation of the silent movement OE of a very bright red-orange luminous phenomenon: observation of a Thai lantern.
description: On July 14, 2009, at 11:10 PM on the beach, a witness observed a very bright, reddish-orange luminous object moving silently in the clear sky. It disappeared over the horizon. The description of the phenomenon—reddish-orange in color, slow speed (observation duration of 10 minutes), and a linear trajectory aligned with the prevailing wind that evening—strongly suggests the possibility of a festive aerial lantern (known as a "Thae" lantern). When contacted about the exact location of the observation, the witness stated: "I later realized that this unidentified flying object was in fact a type of Chinese lantern, which was not identifiable in the night." Following confirmation from the witness, this case is classified as Class A, as it is a typical sighting of a Thae lantern, a common occurrence on July 14th.

summary: Probable sighting of flying lanterns.
description: On July 14, 2009, at approximately 11:45 PM, a witness observed red lights in the sky moving at a constant speed 150 meters above the ground. No sound was heard during the 10-second observation. These lights, which formed a V shape, disappeared into a cloud. Numerous similar sightings have been reported in the local press. This witness likely observed sky lanterns, which are currently very popular, especially during festive events.

summary: Observation of the random movement of a bright, spherical white phenomenon in the sky: lack of information.
description: Recent report (December 19, 2011) of an earlier observation from July 14, 2009, around 1:30 a.m.: through a skylight, a person observed for a long time the random movement of a very bright, white, spherical object in the sky. The witness heard no unusual noises. No other reports were collected. Of moderate strangeness but lacking sufficient evidence (brief description, only one witness), this observation is difficult to conclude. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the passage of flying lanterns.
description: On the night of July 4-5, 2009, several people observed lights in the sky from a garden. These lights moved slowly and silently in a V-shaped formation. They then disappeared abruptly. The police investigation determined that the lights came from approximately fifty Chinese lanterns released from a nearby golf course for a wedding celebration.

summary: Observation of a luminous disk passing at a rapid and constant speed without any noise. Probable atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.
description: On Saturday, July 4, 2009, at approximately 11:40 PM, a witness observed a luminous disc silently passing across the sky for two to three seconds. The disc moved in a straight line at very high speed, following a trajectory from Bordeaux to Perpignan. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. This observation of a very bright disc crossing the sky in a few seconds suggests the atmospheric reentry of a meteorite. However, the witness did not observe a green or yellow trail, as expected in such cases. It is possible that the witness's night vision was not very good, given their age. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.

summary: Observation of luminous phenomena that move and change direction: lack of information
description: On July 4, 2009, between approximately 12:30 and 12:43 AM, a witness in a parking lot observed a luminous phenomenon above a neighboring building for two to three minutes. The sky was clear, and the witness described whitish fireballs. The phenomenon moved silently along a south-south trajectory, then stopped and changed direction before rapidly disappearing to the east. The witness filmed the scene on their cell phone. Unfortunately, the videos of this event are unusable, as are the two photographs extracted by the witness from the video. No other reports were collected by GEIPAN regarding the observation of this phenomenon. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Observations of the successive appearance and movement of white lights in the sky: lack of information.
description: On July 4, 2009, around 1:00 AM, four people observed two large white lights in the sky. These lights quickly disappeared, followed by three smaller lights that moved off in different directions. One witness reported that these three lights formed a triangular shape in the sky. No noise was heard during the 15-minute observation. The witness went to the police station. However, GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) only received one witness statement by email. The observation took place during the night from Friday to Saturday, around 1:00 AM. The described characteristics of two white lights followed by three smaller lights with fluctuating trajectories, moving silently, could lead to the possible hypothesis of flying lanterns. Nevertheless, the early date of the observation and the lack of information (despite the witness's willingness to cooperate) prevent further investigation. This case is classified in category C: lack of information.

summary: Recurrent observations of light phenomena.
description: A witness and his wife, living in a country house, have observed occasional or recurring phenomena near their home for several years: luminous orbs of varying sizes, sometimes distant, sometimes close, moving about. Following the observations of experts sent to the witnesses, it became clear that the luminous orbs they observed every evening were stars or planets. The brightest was Jupiter, which rose in the east around 7:30 PM at the end of October 2011. As for the other supposed observations above their field of vision, no evidence was found to either confirm or refute the witness's claims. GEIPAN classifies the recurring observations (Jupiter and stars) as category A and the other observations as category C. The case is therefore classified overall as category C.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a square shape with bright spots at the extremities.
description: A witness reports that one evening (around 11 p.m.) in July 2009, while on his terrace, he heard the sound of an engine and saw a dark, square shape with four points of light pass overhead. Frightened, he went inside but watched the object slowly move southward before it disappeared, hidden behind the neighboring house. The recent questionnaire (dated January 19, 2011) about this earlier sighting provides few details and makes any investigation impossible. No other similar accounts from this area have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information (the date of the sighting is arbitrarily given as the first day of the month).

summary: Sighting of a dark "flying plate". Sudden turn to 45th.
description: motorist reported by telephone that he saw a dark, flying object move near Compiègne, making a turn and disappearing in the direction of Lille. The witness heard no noise. Despite repeated inquiries, no further information regarding the precise location, position, duration, or any additional details about its characteristics, nor any official report, has been received by GEIPAN (the French National Police Intervention Group). The case is classified as Class C due to lack of information.

summary: Observing lights in the night.
description: Email report from several witnesses of an observation of multiple lights (approximately 7 to 8) at 1:15 AM on Saturday night/Sunday morning. The main witness does not wish to complete the questionnaire provided by GEIPAN, nor even file a report with the police. Any investigation is impossible due to a lack of more precise information. Observation classified as C due to insufficient information.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon with a change in speed and sudden disappearance: lack of information.
description: On June 28, 2009, at approximately 4:30 a.m., campers were intrigued by the movement of luminous phenomena in the sky. Only one report was sent to GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena). The movements described by the objects are difficult to relate to the usual sources of misinterpretation, with the exception of nightclub spotlights, but these are primarily observed in overcast weather, not under clear skies. In any case, their operation is rarely limited to a few tens of seconds. This observation presents a high level of strangeness and would merit a thorough investigation to confirm its validity. GEIPAN actively attempted to contact the witness without success. This strange case remains inconclusive due to the single report and the lack of an investigation. This case is provisionally classified as Class C, pending any further information.

summary: Observation of the movement of about fifty luminous orange balls.
description: witness reported by telephone that he observed approximately fifty orange luminous orbs passing by between 11:55 a.m. and midnight on the night of June 27, 2009. According to him, other witnesses in his building made the same observation. Although the description of the large number of orange luminous orbs suggests the possibility of flying lanterns, an investigation is impossible due to a lack of further information (no completed questionnaire, no police report), despite repeated attempts to contact the witness.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On June 26, 2009, at approximately 11:30 PM, two witnesses observed a very bright and intriguing phenomenon from their homes. One witness sent us a photograph taken from a video recorded during the observation. The description of the object's silent, ascending trajectory from the ground, the duration of the observation, and its brightness all point to a genuine sighting that would have benefited from further details. Unfortunately, despite repeated requests, no additional information has been received, making any investigation impossible.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: observation of an aircraft.
description: On June 20, 2009, at approximately 7:20 PM, a witness filmed a puzzling phenomenon: a bright point of light moving silently across the sky. Reviewing the video clearly shows a misidentification of an aircraft departing from or approaching Saint-Pierre Pierrefonds Airport (Réunion Island): green navigation lights and flashing anti-collision lights. This is a Class A case: aircraft sighting.

summary: Observation of the globular cluster M13 and subsequent observation on photos of a red dot and line: lack of information.
description: On June 18, 2009, between 11:59 PM and 12:13 AM, an amateur astronomer photographed the star cluster M13. He was then surprised to notice a point with a red line on several of his photographs, which seemed to indicate the movement of an object. The witness did not make a direct observation. He sent the original raw images, but these were unfortunately lost due to a computer failure. This case of astronomical observation is unusual. The movement observed over about fifteen minutes seems to rule out the usual satellites in low Earth orbit with very rapid relative motion. The Amazns BrzTank satellite (likely a large piece of debris) could be a good candidate; its brightness can vary if it is rotating, like most uncontrolled satellites. However, its angular velocity of 1.89 arcminutes/s would cause it to move by approximately 28 arcseconds during the 15-minute image sequence, which is not the case, as it remains within the telescope's field of view. It could also be an asteroid passing close to Earth; this latter hypothesis seems unlikely, especially since the observed area is far from the ecliptic, where most of these objects orbit. GEIPAN did not have the raw images for this analysis. An optical or photographic artifact (internal or external reflections) is also a possibility. GEIPAN classifies this case as C due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent passage of a green ball on a downward trajectory: probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: During a patrol on June 15, 2009, at 10:40 PM, two soldiers spotted a green ball silently passing by on a descending trajectory. The phenomenon disappeared abruptly over the horizon. This observation of a very bright green ball moving in a straight line for 5 to 6 seconds corresponds to the classic testimony of a bolide. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of a meteoroid (meteorite) entering the atmosphere.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a dark triangular shape delimited by lights.
description: On June 12, 2009, at 11:10 PM, a witness observed lights above her, outlining a large, dark, triangular mass moving in a north-south direction without any sound being heard. No other witness statements were collected. The witness described alignments of lights, similar to stars, forming a dark triangle. This triangle moved slowly towards the sea. It is possible that the dark triangle was simply an optical illusion created by the alignment of the points of light, which could be Thai lanterns. The movement of the points could be due solely to the (weak, northwest) wind. The description of the lights and the movement is insufficiently precise for GEIPAN to confirm this hypothesis. This case is classified as "C": insufficient evidence to draw a conclusion.

summary: A posteriori observation of an annular shape on a photograph: no direct observation.
description: The witness took several photos on June 7, 2009, at 1:39 PM on the Caussol plateau. It was only later that he noticed a silvery, ring-shaped object in the upper left corner of one of the photographs. The suspicious object, located in the upper left of the photo, was not seen by the witness. The blurred shape clearly suggests an insect in flight (body and wings visible), probably very close to the camera. The landscape and the season are conducive to insects. GEIPAN classifies this case as "B": probable photograph of a small insect in flight.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a sphere with a metallic appearance.
description: This sighting in June 2009 was reported to GEIPAN only in February 2011. Even though the witness account is not disputed (one main witness and their family) and describes the sighting of "a luminous, metallic-looking sphere," any subsequent verification of a slow-moving phenomenon ("10 km/h, like a weather balloon or similar") is impossible. No other evidence, such as a police report or visual evidence (photos or otherwise), supplements the file. The case is classified as Class C because any investigation is impossible.

summary: Rockfall.
description: On June 3, 2009, a witness observed an object falling, striking a fir tree, and rolling on the ground. The object measured 4.5 x 7.5 centimeters and weighed approximately 300 grams. The witness assumed it was a piece of meteorite. Analysis by a mineralogy expert at the OMP Toulouse Geological Survey's Transfer Mechanisms Laboratory concluded that it was indeed hematite, more commonly known as iron ore, and in no way a celestial body. No impact crater was found at the location where the object fell, and there were no other witnesses to the sighting.

summary: Photograph of light trails left by an airplane.
description: Around 7 p.m. on the evening of June 3rd or 4th, 2009 (the witness doesn't remember the exact date), an amateur photographer took a picture of the sky showing the moon and a white contrail from an airplane. When viewing the photo two days later, he noticed something unusual in the image, something he hadn't seen when he took the picture. This person had photographed a moving airliner, giving the impression of "parallel bars" as described by the witness. In comparison, jet engine contrails appear stationary.

summary: Presence of a light streak on a photograph without direct observation during the shooting: probable observation of a reflection.
description: witness noticed a bright spot in the sky in one of their photos. No direct observation of this spot was made when the photo was taken. No other reports have been received regarding the observation of this phenomenon. The vertical streak is most likely an artifact of the photo and the processing within the camera: The original photo, 5512, had already undergone significant processing in the camera (increased sharpness and high compression rate); the photo named 2009-06-01-Hurbache-01.JPG appears to be an enlarged version where the defects are amplified. The bright spot could be a reflection of the sun on an aircraft, a satellite, or a balloon. GEIPAN classifies this case as B.

summary: Observation of the high-speed and silent passage of an object formed by three orange luminous points: lack of information.
description: On Saturday, May 30, 2009, at approximately 2:50 a.m., a witness on their terrace observed, for three seconds, the rapid and silent passage of an object composed of three orange points of light forming an equilateral triangle. The witness also distinguished a fainter orange halo between these points. No other witness accounts were collected. This case is considered slightly unusual given its very short duration and straight trajectory, but the witness account is, on the other hand, very consistent: the witness is an experienced observer, very precise when possible (direction, wind speed), and refrains from commenting when necessary. The account has several characteristics of fireball sightings, but not enough to definitively confirm that it was one. No confirmation has been found in the BOAM database. This case is classified as Class C due to the lack of other independent witness accounts and corroborating evidence.

summary: Probable astronomical observation of Jupiter.
description: On May 28, 2009, between 4:25 and 4:50 AM, two witnesses observed a stationary and exceptionally bright point in the sky. Photographs were taken of the phenomenon, the brightness of which diminished with sunrise. These witnesses likely made an astronomical observation of Jupiter, which was particularly visible at that time of year (apparent magnitude approximately -2.5 and angular diameter approximately 40").

summary: Observation of a rectangular shape rotating on itself and gaining altitude: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN was contacted by the witness via email on Sunday, February 28, 2010, following the broadcast the previous day of a program on TF1. The observation dates back to Saturday, May 23, 2009. While on vacation, the witness and his family saw a black rectangular object move within their field of vision before disappearing into the distance. The witness sent the Terrestrial Questionnaire on May 12, 2009, almost a year after the event, along with a site plan including the object's trajectory and a drawing of its shape. The characteristics of this observation are somewhat unusual and inconsistent (only one observation report, without a photograph). The observed phenomenon is probably a balloon, but of a very unusual shape. Therefore, and as the lack of reliable weather data prevents verification that the movement of the balloon is consistent with the wind, GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of information.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear West-East movement of a luminous phenomenon, brief zig-zag before disappearance: ISS passage.
description: On Friday, May 22, 2009, at approximately 11:30 PM, two witnesses were intrigued by the west-to-east passage of a white luminous phenomenon with a steady speed. One of the witnesses observed a zigzag pattern made by the phenomenon before it quickly faded. The witnesses most likely observed a pass of the International Space Station (ISS) as it entered Earth's shadow. The brief zigzag observed by one of the witnesses during the observation may be due to an autokinetic phenomenon: focused on the point of light crossing the sky, the brain momentarily lost its bearings and interpreted the natural movements of the eyeballs as a movement of the point of light itself. This case is classified as Class A, observation of a pass of the International Space Station.

summary: Multiple observations of silent movement of luminous phenomena: lack of information.
description: A witness briefly reported several observations made around midnight on May 13, 19, and 22, 2009. He filmed the movement of a luminous phenomenon. No unusual noises were heard. GEIPAN twice requested further information from the witness regarding this case (specifically, the precise location of the observation). These requests went unanswered. Due to a lack of precise information, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C": insufficient information.

summary: Observation of the slow, silent movement of luminous orange balls: lack of information.
description: On May 17, 2009, around 1:00 AM, two people observed about ten orange lights in the sky. They appeared to originate from the same location and all silently moved towards Grange-sur-Lot. They disappeared over the horizon. The witness provided several photographs showing the reconstruction and their positions. Unfortunately, the video recording was not transmitted to GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information and Experimentation on Astronomical Phenomena). No other witness statements were collected. While relatively unfamiliar, this observation, thanks to the detailed testimony, has all the characteristics of a misidentification of a Thai lantern. The lack of precise weather data for the observation site and the absence of records for the region precludes a definitive conclusion. This case is classified as Class C: lack of precise weather information and corroborating evidence to validate the Thai lantern hypothesis.

summary: Recent testimony of an old and fleeting observation of a silent passage of a dark orange triangular shape in the sky: lack of information.
description: Recent report (March 15, 2011) of an earlier observation made on May 13, 2009, at 2:00 AM, lasting 5 to 6 seconds. A witness observed the sky in front of their home and saw a silent, dark orange, V-shaped object pass very quickly. The object emitted no apparent blinking and disappeared rapidly. The witness made a similar observation in September, but this time they observed two similar objects flying together, again silently. This case is relatively strange, but the short duration of the observation, the lack of detail due to a very late report, and the absence of independent witness statements make its credibility very weak and preclude any conclusion. This case is classified as Class C due to the lack of independent witness statements and corroborating evidence.

summary: Observation of black teche's in photographs without direct observation during the shooting: probable photograph of insects or birds.
description: witness contacted GEIPAN on January 10, 2010, regarding a photograph taken on May 12, 2009, containing seven black dots that the witness could not identify. This case of observation, lacking direct observation at the time the photograph was taken, is of minor strangeness and inconsistent evidence, bearing all the hallmarks of a case of mistaken identity involving a flock of insects or possibly birds. Verification of civil and military air traffic therefore seems unnecessary; in any case, it is difficult more than a month after the event. This case is classified as Class B: insect or bird flight in a photograph.

summary: Observations of the rapid passage of a luminous white ball: straight trajectory SW-NE. Probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.
description: On May 10, 2009, at 2:58 a.m., two people in a vehicle observed the rapid passage of a white sphere surrounded by a faint halo. The phenomenon moved along a straight southwest-northeast trajectory before disappearing completely. The observation lasted a few seconds. Of low strangeness and very good consistency, this observation has all the characteristics of a meteoroid reentry. However, the lack of other eyewitness accounts prevents a firm conclusion. This case is classified as Class B: probable observation of a bolide (atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid).

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a triangular flying object: lack of information.
description: On May 3, 2009, at approximately 10:15 PM, a witness was intrigued by the silent passage of an object over his home. Flashing white lights at each corner outlined a dark triangular shape to the witness, and a steady red light was also observed. The witness then called his partner, who could only make out two white lights and one non-flashing red light moving away into the sky. The first witness followed the object with his eyes for about four to five minutes. No other witness statements were collected. No civilian aircraft were reported in the airspace of the towns mentioned by the witness. After investigation, considering the police report, the evidence gathered, the site visits, the witness interview, and the research conducted, this case appears to be complex, as it reveals three distinct phases of observation that are not necessarily linked. Furthermore, the evidence is somewhat inconsistent, as the sole witness's account is not always coherent (the lengthy investigation is undoubtedly a significant contributing factor). The husband's testimony is noted, but it only pertains to the end of the observation, the least unusual phase. It is troubling that the witness makes no mention of the moon, which was clearly within his field of vision: it is almost certain that the moon played a role in the phenomenon, although it is impossible to say precisely how. However, this cannot explain the steady red light observed by both witnesses. A complex scenario involving fireworks followed by a misinterpretation of the moon through clouds coinciding with a passing aircraft could be considered, but several factors are inconsistent. Given these uncertainties, and without being able to definitively establish that this phenomenon is truly unusual, GEIPAN classifies this case as Category C due to a lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of aircraft flying at very low altitude and displaying white and red lights: lack of information.
description: On May 2, 2009, between 11:00 PM and midnight, a witness in his garden observed the rapid passage of objects flying at very low altitude and displaying white and red lights. No further documentation was produced despite a request for a ground questionnaire and for the witness statement to be filed with the Gendarmerie. It is very difficult to draw conclusions from such a small amount of information. The strangeness of the case is relatively low, as is its consistency (only one witness, no detailed questionnaire, no photos or videos). This case is classified as C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon: observation of the passage of the International Space Station (ISS)
description: On April 25, 2009, at 5:10 AM, a witness observed a very bright, silent southwest-northeast passing of a ball across the sky. The trajectory was straight, and the speed was fast and steady. Unfortunately, the photographs taken were unusable. After verification with the station's orbital reports (Space-track), this observation undoubtedly corresponds to a pass of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon by an amateur astronomer: variations in color and magnitude. Lack of information.
description: On April 22, 2009, at 4:45 a.m., an amateur astronomer was intrigued by a stationary object in the sky with strong color variations (green, red, blue) and a variable magnitude (sharp increase followed by decrease). According to the witness, the event lasted 15 seconds. This observation strongly suggests a temporary reflection on a satellite: a flash from an Iridium satellite, or a reflection on a rotating satellite. Despite its requests, GEIPAN (the French National Astronomical Society) has not received further details and cannot verify this hypothesis too long after the event. This unusual case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Successive observations of a very bright light in the sky: astronomical observation of the planet Venus
description: witness reported seeing a bright light due east in the sky at sunrise. The witness sent two photographs. After astronomical verification, this observation was confirmed to be the planet Venus. This case is therefore classified as "A," meaning it has been definitively identified.

summary: Observation by several witnesses of the movement of white objects in the sky.
description: On April 9, 2009, in the early afternoon, four witnesses at an airfield observed the slow movement of white, spherical objects in the sky. No noise was heard during the observation. The phenomenon gradually disappeared from view. Following the testimony of two people and the subsequent investigation, no formal explanation for this observation was found, but the possibility of scientific balloons is favored despite the lack of confirmation from Swiss meteorological services and laboratories. The case is classified as "B".

summary: Observation of the passage of an ovoid balloon filled with helium.
description: On April 4, 2009, at 11:00 AM, two pedestrians observed a large, gray, oval-shaped object in a cloudy sky, oscillating on its axis. The observation lasted five minutes, after which the witnesses saw the object move without hearing any noise: no trail was observed. The object gradually disappeared to the east. On April 10, GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) received an email from a journalist who had an anonymous photo of a UFO, which he claimed had been taken around noon on April 4 at Roissy Airport, and which he was trying to analyze. Analysis of the photograph showed that it was indeed taken on April 4, 2009, at 9:22 AM. However, further investigation revealed that the photo was not taken from Roissy Airport but in the vicinity of taxiways W2, F3, or V2 at Le Bourget Airport. Indeed, an enlargement of the photograph reveals the logo of a company that owns a hangar at Le Bourget Airport. Finally, the gendarmerie investigation established that on April 4, 2009, at 11:00 AM, the control tower at Le Bourget Airport reported the presence of an inflatable balloon shaped like a flying saucer north of the airfield, outside the airport zone. The object, neutralized and taken into custody by the local police, turned out to be a 20-meter diameter balloon intended for use as entertainment during a sporting event at the Stade de France.

summary: Observation of the rapid zigzag passage and SW of a white light with a reddish glow: lack of information.
description: On April 2, 2009, at approximately 11:10 PM, a witness observed a white, reddish-brown, pinhead-shaped phenomenon in a cloudy sky. This phenomenon moved very rapidly in a zigzag pattern from south to west, appearing to fall towards the Pyrenees. The lack of information (questionnaire or police report) prevented an investigation or the development of hypotheses. Therefore, GEIPAN classified this case as Category C due to insufficient information.

summary: Observation of the movement of two circular objects in the sky.
description: Several witnesses observed two bright red, spherical objects moving in a straight line around 10:23 PM on April 1, 2009. No noise was heard during the observation. The objects gradually disappeared into the distance. The characteristics described by the witnesses—several luminous points moving along the same trajectory, following the wind direction, at low altitude and moderate speed (20 km/h)—support the hypothesis of flying light balloons similar to Thai lanterns. However, in the absence of a police report and therefore no official record, a thorough investigation is not possible. These observations are thus classified as Category C due to insufficient information.

summary: Observation in a break in dark clouds of the successive passage of three very bright white disks followed by a dark red phenomenon: lack of information.
description: In October 2010, a person reported an observation made on April 1, 2009. At 6:45 a.m., a witness, from an open window, observed, through a break in the dark, cloudy sky, the passage of three white, circular phenomena, identical in size, speed, and trajectory, at three-second intervals. A dark red shape then appeared, leading the witness to believe they were seeing fire. The sky then cleared very rapidly. No unusual noises were heard during the continuous observation, which lasted approximately twenty seconds. Only one witness account was collected. The strangeness of this case is difficult to assess given the unusual description of the observed phenomenon. Its credibility remains weak in the absence of corroborating evidence and independent testimonies. However, given that the observation area is located within a very busy military flight path, the hypothesis of military aircraft is likely, but some elements remain difficult to explain (total absence of noise, thin red line behind the phenomenon). Unfortunately, the lack of available data after three years regarding any potential activity prevents us from concluding with certainty that this is the case. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of independent eyewitness accounts and corroboration.

summary: Observation of a stationary sphere in the sky. A dull metallic noise was heard just before the observation.
description: On March 30, 2009, at 11:50 AM, a witness observed fighter jets in the sky. Suddenly, a dull metallic noise was heard. The witness then saw a stationary, grayish-white metallic sphere in the sky. It was larger than the aircraft. This sphere disappeared and reappeared a few seconds later. The frightened witness then went home. This poorly documented 2009 observation was only recently submitted to the panel of experts working with GEIPAN for analysis. The correlation between the noise reported by the witness and the observation is not clear. Air navigation data is unavailable (military maneuvers? aircraft movements?...) although the observation was made along the runway of the nearby airbase, and it is common for military aircraft to 'check' flying objects in their airspace. In the absence of a thorough investigation, this case, which is inconsistent and lacks any unusual characteristics, is classified in category "C".

summary: Observation of a UFO filmed by an automatic video recording station: probable atmospheric reentry.
description: witness provided two videos to the police, recorded by an automatic video recording station on March 30, 2009, at 2:38 PM. The first video, filmed at 2:34 PM (video M20090330_123414_LINER), shows the trail of an airliner. The second video (video M20090330_123824_PAN) shows the passage of an unknown, shimmering object. This rare case of a daytime video recording (M20090330_123824_PAN) of a luminous trail suggests a meteor. However, its apparent speed (angular velocity) seems slow for a meteor compared to the angular velocity of the airliner, recorded with the same device. This relative slowness can be explained as follows: since it is daytime and the sky is partially overcast, only the brightest part of the trajectory can be observed, which is the end of a meteor's path, when the object is slowed down the most by the atmosphere. Another uncertainty regarding this meteor hypothesis is that it is only acceptable if the cloud cover is considered sufficiently transparent, as the luminous phenomenon associated with a meteor physically occurs above 10 km in altitude. The video of the aircraft's contrail (probably at over 3000 m) seems to confirm this hypothesis, but without certainty. The witness will send GEIPAN another video taken on May 4, 2009: it shows the movement of a ball of light along an upward trajectory, for which GEIPAN currently has no explanation (video M20090504_162251).

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a luminous phenomenon with a trail. Sudden disappearance: probable observation of a bolide.
description: On March 30, 2009, at 5:10 PM, a family in a car was intrigued by the rapid and silent passage of a luminous phenomenon that followed a straight trajectory across the sky. Ovoid-shaped, light green, and very bright, the phenomenon was followed by a silvery trail. This observation has the characteristics of a bolide (the re-entry of a meteoroid into the atmosphere). Unfortunately, the lack of other eyewitness accounts prevents confirmation of this hypothesis. This case is classified as Class B: observation of a bolide, probably due to the re-entry of a meteoroid (meteorite).

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon.
description: On March 28, 2009, at 8:00 PM, a person observed a luminous phenomenon in the northern sky. They described a very bright star moving slowly from west to east along a curved path. This witness used binoculars during the observation. No further details were provided by the witness about this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the movement of a white ball.
description: On March 25, 2009, between 8:43 and 8:44 a.m., two hikers observed a large white sphere moving at low altitude before disappearing behind the Dent de Rez mountain range. In a letter dated April 3, 2009, the witness confirmed that the photographed object was indeed a signal sphere, but that he also saw something else: it could have been Venus, visible near the eastern horizon that day. Accurately measuring the sphere's movement by aligning it with fixed objects would have resolved this possibility. However, since the precise observation point is unknown, this hypothesis cannot be confirmed.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a luminous yellow-orange ball and its sudden disappearance: lack of information.
description: On March 22, 2009, at approximately 8:45 PM, two people were intrigued by a yellow sphere passing silently at low altitude in the sky. The witnesses observed the phenomenon begin to zigzag laterally and rapidly in short bursts, turn orange, and then quickly disappear. Only one witness account was collected. Aside from the changes in direction, the account strongly resembles the observation of atmospheric reentry of debris from a satellite or meteor, or a festive lantern. This observation is of a medium level of strangeness, but the overall consistency does not allow for a D1 classification. This case is classified as Class C due to a lack of independent and corroborating witness accounts.

summary: Observation of a white luminous streak on a photograph without direct observation: probable passage of an insect.
description: On the evening of March 21, 2009, under a clear, cloudless sky, a witness had their photograph taken. Upon viewing the digital photo, the witness was intrigued by a white streak in the sky. Since there was no direct observation of anything during the photograph, the prevailing hypothesis is that an insect or a small bird passed close to the subject at the moment the flash was triggered. The insect would have been intensely illuminated by the flash. This case is classified as "B": probable passage of an insect through the camera's field of view.

summary: Observation of about ten luminous orbs in the sky.
description: witness observed approximately ten luminous orbs crossing the sky at around 8:45 PM on March 18, 2009, moving from south to north along the Saene. The characteristics of the observation (ten luminous orbs) correspond to the known phenomenon of sky lanterns. In the absence of further information requested, this hypothesis cannot be confirmed. No other eyewitness accounts have been collected regarding this phenomenon, for which we lack information.

summary: Observation of the American space shuttle approaching the ISS.
description: On March 17, 2009, at approximately 8:10 PM, a witness observed two luminous white discs moving east-northeast, seemingly connected by a mass. During the day, at the time of the observation, the space shuttle was in its approach phase to the International Space Station (ISS). The witness's testimony is consistent with the observation of this "twin-link." This case is classified as "A": observation of the shuttle approaching the ISS.

summary: Observation of the passage of two bright points: probable observation of the space shuttle and the ISS.
description: On the first day, at the time of the observation, the space shuttle was in its approach phase to the International Space Station. The following day, the shuttle had docked with the ISS. The witness's account is consistent with the observation of this "towing," except that the witness describes a change of direction. Since this change of direction occurred behind a cloud (a chimney), it is possible that the direction of movement was misjudged. The changes in brightness and appearance are normal: the reflection of the sun varies during the pass, and approaching the horizon gives a reddish appearance to all bright objects. This case is classified as "B": probable observation of the space shuttle and the ISS.

summary: Long observations of a bright point appearing to follow the Moon: astronomical observations of Antares.
description: On March 17, 2009, at 2:20 a.m., a witness observed a bright point near the Moon, which intrigued him. At work, he and his colleagues made this observation several more times. The intensity of the bright point disappeared with sunrise. The position of the point and its movement puzzled the witnesses. The astronomical configuration clearly shows that the witnesses observed the star Antares. This star "follows" the Moon and appears to revolve around it, as described by one of the witnesses. This apparent natural movement is simply due to the relative distances between the star and the Moon, and to the Earth's rotation.

summary: Observation of the space shuttle and the International Space Station (ISS)
description: witness reports observing two bright points of light slowly passing across the sky. They moved southward, parallel to each other and maintaining the same distance. No sound was heard during the brief observation before the objects disappeared. On the day and at the time of the observation, the space shuttle was in its approach phase to the International Space Station. The witness's testimony is consistent with the observation of this "tug-of-war." However, it should be noted that the direction described by the witness (southward) is not consistent with the "Pointe des Corbeaux" direction he also indicates, which is E-SE, consistent with the ISS's trajectory (see map). This case is classified as "A": observation of the space shuttle + ISS

summary: Watching the space shuttle and the ISS pass overhead.
description: A witness reported an observation made on March 17, 2009, between 8:10 PM and 8:15 PM. They observed two bright white points of light moving northward at a constant speed from west to east along a straight trajectory. At the time of the observation, the space shuttle was in its approach phase to the International Space Station. The witness's testimony is consistent with the observation of this "coordinated" object. This case is classified as "A": observation of the space shuttle and the ISS.

summary: quick observation of a luminous disc. No noise.
description: On March 15, 2009, at approximately 10:15 PM, a witness was intrigued by the sight of a very bright, ionized circle that remained motionless above the ridge of his roof. This object disappeared after a rapid reduction in size. No noise was heard during this observation, which lasted about four seconds. No other sightings or festive activities in the area were reported. It was noted that the planet Saturn was very close to the indicated direction and was particularly bright at that time (magnitude 0.64, meaning slightly brighter than the stars of the Big Dipper). However, the witness described a disk, whereas Saturn appears as a point of light to the naked eye, even for a witness with very good eyesight. The disappearance also raises questions, but the photograph of the observation site shows a tree between the observer and the sky; movement of the witness or a tree branch could have caused an occultation of the planet. These two questions mean that this case is classified as C.

summary: Observation of the silent SN movement of lights outlining a "V-shape": lack of information
description: On Saturday, March 14, 2009, between 10:00 PM and 10:05 PM, a person on their terrace was intrigued by the regular, south-south movement of a group of lights outlining a "V-shape." The observation was very brief, and the witness noticed no unusual noise. The most plausible hypothesis (a low-flying aircraft or a formation of military aircraft) was deemed insufficient (due to its appearance and silence); GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group) was unable to submit the necessary verification requests to air traffic control in time. A field investigation conducted several years later would have yielded very little reliable information. Lacking these verifications, this case is classified as Class C due to insufficient information.

summary: Observation of the movement of three luminous points forming a triangle.
description: This case corresponds to an observation made on March 13, 2009, and reported to GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information on Astronomical Phenomena) via a questionnaire on January 6, 2010, ten months later. On March 13, 2009, around 7:00 PM, a witness observed three white-orange lights moving together to form an equilateral triangle. One of the lights was flashing. No unusual noises were heard during the observation. The entire display quickly disappeared into the clouds. No other reports were collected regarding this phenomenon, and unfortunately, due to the late date of the report, any search for a radar trace could not be initiated. The description of the phenomenon (3 luminous points moving together, one of which was "flashing"), the trajectory described by the witness (point 1 and point 2 at the end of the runway at Lognes-Emerainville aerodrome) which corresponds to the visual landing corridor of this aerodrome, strongly suggest the probable observation of an aircraft approaching the aerodrome.

summary: Observation of the slow and silent movement of a black triangular object delimited by colored and flashing lights: lack of information.
description: On March 3, 2009, at approximately 8:30 PM, four people in a car on a country road were intrigued by the slow movement of three flashing, colored lights in the sky, outlining a triangular object. The low-altitude object disappeared behind a hill; no unusual noise was heard during the observation. Only one witness report was filed. Due to its linear movement and its partially aircraft-like appearance (flashing lights and a red light), the phenomenon was considered relatively unremarkable. It is possible that the triangular shape described by the witness was simply the smallest possible form encompassing the three points of light. As the witness report came more than a month after the event, the radar records of civil and military aviation are no longer accessible. The imprecision of the witness's report regarding the direction of the trajectory and the size of the phenomenon relative to known landmarks prevents any conclusions from being drawn about its exact nature. For these various reasons, this case is classified as Class C due to a lack of information.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On February 28th, at approximately 9:45 PM, a witness looked up at the sky and suddenly saw a fireball followed by a yellow flame cross horizontally from west to east. The observation lasted two to three seconds. Despite the lack of information, the described characteristics correspond to a probable atmospheric reentry.

summary: Multiple observations of rapid movement of luminous phenomena in the sky. Lack of information.
description: A witness reported several sightings of ovoid luminous phenomena moving back and forth in the sky. All these sightings occurred between 2:15 and 3:50 a.m. The very late receipt of the police report made an investigation impossible, particularly regarding the search for any aircraft or helicopters that might have been present in the area at that time.

summary: Observation of two luminous objects in a mountain range.
description: On February 28, 2009, between 6:30 PM and 7:35 PM, people at a ski resort observed two spherical lights of different sizes from various locations. The observations were made from a considerable distance, but witnesses noted the movement of these bright spheres within the mountain range. Numerous photos and videos of the phenomenon were taken before the lights disappeared. This observation was reported very late to GEIPAN (March 4, 2011) through a questionnaire and a large number of photos. Without conducting a thorough investigation, the reconstruction of the observation based on two of the photos (IMG_0114 and IMG_0105) places the phenomenon ("two luminous spheres") on the mountainside near the ski slopes. The observation period coincided with the peak ski season. The hypothesis of observing the headlights/projectors (one of the 2 balls) of a ski slope maintenance vehicle (snow groomer) and an inflatable lighting balloon (a commonly used technique) is probable.

summary: Observation of the peculiar and silent movement of a red luminous phenomenon: probable observation of aircraft in formation.
description: A witness observed two red lights in the sky on February 27, 2009, at approximately 8:48 PM. The lights moved silently in a circle and then moved away to the south. The witness reported another observation on August 15, 2009. The observation described by the witness is entirely consistent with the appearance of two military aircraft flying in formation. This case is classified as Class B, indicating the probable observation of a military aircraft patrol.

summary: Observation of the movement of a colored luminous phenomenon: probable observation of a bolide (meteoroid fall).
description: On Friday, February 20, 2009, at approximately 7:00 AM, a motorist observed a blue/green luminous phenomenon passing from northwest to southeast in the sky. We were unable to verify this report with the database of amateur meteor observers or with the French meteor observation network. Nevertheless, the characteristics reported by the witness are entirely consistent with an atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid. This case is classified as Class B, like the probable observation of a bolide (meteoroid fall).

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of a luminous orange ball: lack of information.
description: On Sunday, February 15, 2009, around 8:00 PM, two people in a car spotted a luminous orange ball in the sky moving quite quickly. The observation lasted a few seconds before the phenomenon disappeared. This case could have been compared to the one in Hautefort on the same day, almost at the same time (30 minutes earlier), but the witness did not fill out a questionnaire, and we have no details to draw any conclusions. The witness mentioned a possible fireball impact (meteorite fall), but we do not know the direction of the phenomenon's trajectory. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a very bright white light: probable observation of a meteoroid reentry.
description: On February 15, 2009, at approximately 7:30 PM, a witness observed the rapid passage of a bright white phenomenon at low altitude. The phenomenon disappeared, hidden by the landscape. No unusual noise was heard during the observation, which lasted less than five seconds. We interpret the witness's description of a light shaped like a toadstool as a bright object followed by a trail. The very short observation time, combined with a linear trajectory, strongly suggests a highly probable observation of an atmospheric reentry of a bolide. This case, characterized by its low strangeness and lack of consistency, is classified as "B": probable misidentification as a meteor reentry.

summary: Observation of the passage of an incandescent object across the sky: lack of information.
description: On February 15, 2009, between 10:20 and 10:30 PM, a person was intrigued by a high-pitched, shrill noise that stopped abruptly. Joined by her husband, the couple then observed through the window the straight passage across the sky of an incandescent object, first red, then orange. The object followed a downward trajectory and was quickly obscured by vegetation. The gendarmerie conducted an investigation with various sky monitoring organizations: no incident or sudden loss of altitude was observed on the night in question. This case presents a certain strangeness, but it is difficult to go beyond the investigation conducted by the gendarmerie. The observation period seems too long for a fireball resulting from a meteoroid fall, and an atmospheric reentry of space debris from east to west is highly improbable. The noise heard from inside the house is the most disturbing element and one that we cannot relate to any usual hypothesis. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Astronomical observation of Venus.
description: On February 11, 2009, at approximately 8:20 PM, a witness observed a particularly bright star due west. Viewed first through binoculars and then with a camcorder's zoom lens, the object intrigued the witness. A few days later, in a different location, the witness made a similar observation. The witness observed the planet Venus, particularly visible at that time of year, first with the naked eye and then with a camcorder.

summary: Prolonged observation of an intense and stationary light in the sky: probable observation of Venus.
description: On February 9, 2009, between 8:00 PM and 10:00 PM, several people witnessed a frightening luminous phenomenon. Only one witness reported seeing a large, multicolored glow that remained stationary in the sky. No noise was heard during this two-hour observation. A similar sighting occurred on February 5, 2009, also in the same area. Of low strangeness and moderate consistency (brief witness account, very poor quality photograph), this case presents the characteristics of an astronomical misinterpretation (a luminous object that remained stationary for two hours). Several converging details suggest the possibility of mistaking the planet Venus, but the lack of concrete information, particularly the direction of observation, prevents any formal identification of the UFO. This case is classified as Class B, probable astronomical misinterpretation, with the Venus hypothesis being the most likely.

summary: Observation of the rapid passage of a luminous point alternating between yellow and red. Very rapid speed.
description: A witness briefly reported observing a bright spot in the sky over Blagnac for 3 to 4 minutes, alternating between yellow and red. It gradually disappeared over the Bouconne forest. The witness did not respond to the request for a police report, making any meaningful investigation impossible.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: A witness observed a fireball descending in the overcast sky at 10:00 AM on February 11, 2009. The police, notified, found no fire or debris in the area where the fireball landed. No damage to property or injuries were reported in the area, and no other similar phenomena were observed that same day. The brief witness described a "fireball, colorless and without brightness, descending like a parachute." These characteristics are consistent with the likely observation of atmospheric reentry.

summary: Long observation of a very bright and stationary glow: mistaken for the planet Venus.
description: On February 5, 2009, between 8:45 and 9:00 PM, a motorist observed an intense glow in the sky. Intrigued, he pulled over and took pictures of the UFO with his camera. The observation lasted between 10 and 12 minutes, during which the UFO appeared stationary. The UFO sighting was the subject of press articles in the newspapers L'Est Eclair and Liberation Champagne. While not particularly strange, the reports were sufficiently consistent (numerous coherent and precise details lending credibility to the case, including photographs). This case turned out to be a classic case of mistaken identity involving a well-known astronomical object: the planet Venus. Furthermore, Venus was indeed present in the observed area of the sky, even though the witness did not mention it, and it was particularly bright. The issue was not the witness's visual perception, but rather the witness's interpretation of the observation based on their feelings (surprise, night driving). This case is class A, misunderstanding with the planet Venus.

summary: Observations of a very slow movement of three lights: blue, white and red, each color forming a triangle: lack of information.
description: On February 5, 2009, around 7:00 PM, two people in a car observed three blue, white, and red lights above the four-lane highway. These lights formed a triangle, floating 30 to 40 meters above the ground and moving slowly. GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) received only one witness statement by email. The observation was made through the windshield of a moving car. The weather conditions—it was raining heavily—did not rule out the possibility of reflections. The witness did not respond to GEIPAN's requests for further information (particularly regarding police reports). Therefore, any investigation is impossible due to a lack of information.

summary: Successive observations of movements of bright, red-orange shapes.
description: witness reports two observations made from their kitchen on the 9th floor, looking northwest. On February 4, 2009, at 2:45 a.m., the witness observed the unusual movements of colored shapes that quickly disappeared over the horizon. On February 8, 2009, at 6:45 a.m., the witness and their son observed the upward and then downward movement of a reddish-orange sphere. The first UAP observed, reddish-orange in color, crossed the witness's field of vision from southeast to northwest, in the direction of the prevailing wind: a festive lantern (known as a "Thae lantern") could possibly explain this observation. The second UAP observed appeared directly in the direction of the moon, which was not mentioned by the witness. Its red and changing appearance may have confused the witness at that late hour. For the main observation (UAP ne2), GEIPAN classifies the case as A: observation of the moon at sunset, partially obscured by clouds. For the other observations, these would be classifications of C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of several orange lights forming a triangle: lack of information.
description: GEIPAN was contacted by email on July 7, 2010, by a witness who briefly described an old sighting that occurred on February 3, 2009, between 7:00 and 7:15 PM. The witness, walking down a street, was intrigued by the passage of several ovoid, orange lights that moved silently in a triangular formation. The witness lost sight of the phenomenon as it gradually moved away. While initially appearing rather strange (one might immediately think of a Thai lantern release during festivities following the Chinese New Year, which begins on January 29), this sighting proved more complex because the observed lights were moving against the wind. However, the testimony remained weak due to numerous inaccuracies and the significant time gap between its submission and the event (17 months), which precluded any request to air traffic control. This case is class C due to a lack of additional information.

summary: Atmospheric reentry of a meteorite.
description: Numerous accounts of this atmospheric reentry of a meteorite (bolide of magnitude -10) on January 25, 2009 around 21:22 UTC (22:22 local time) have reached GEIPAN and various websites (see the REFORME network file: Bolide 25janvier2009_21h22TU.pdf).

summary: Observations of luminous phenomena, photographs: photographic artifacts.
description: A witness reported successive sightings (between January 23 and February 2, 2009) of luminous points. The witness provided several dozen photos to support their testimony. These nighttime photos were taken with a flash. None of them show anything unusual, but orbs (dust particles illuminated by the flash) are visible in the vast majority of them. The witness likely exaggerated the description and interpretation of their observations. See an example of orbs and an explanation at /index.php?id=374. GEIPAN classifies this case as "A": a fully identified phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On January 25, 2009, at 6:30 PM, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky. A very bright light moved very quickly along an irregular trajectory. This person likely observed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On January 25, 2009, around 6:30 PM, a motorist observed a red phenomenon with a long trail illuminating the sky. No sound was heard. The witness went to the beach where other witnesses, like himself, seemed to have seen the object fall into the sea. No further witness accounts were collected. All these people likely witnessed an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Astronomical observation of Venus.
description: On February 25, 2009, around 7:00 PM, several people observed a curious luminous phenomenon in the sky from their homes. One of the witnesses filmed the phenomenon, which, upon zooming in, appeared as a luminous sphere with a blue halo, moving in circles. The main witness reported that the phenomenon recurred in the early evenings of the following days. The phenomenon observed (for several consecutive days) and filmed (for several minutes) was none other than the planet Venus, a conclusion recorded in the police report and confirmed by the main witness. The very bright planet Venus (magnitude -4.5) was indeed in the area of the sky observed and filmed by the witness.

summary: Observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon which splits into several flashes: probable observation of a bolide (fall of a meteor or space debris).
description: On January 19, 2009, at 6:46 PM, a witness was intrigued by a bright yellow light moving across the sky that separated into several distinct yellow/red glows. The phenomenon quickly faded. The observation lasted between 10 and 15 seconds. The characteristics reported by the witness leave little doubt as to the nature of the phenomenon, consistent with the witness's second intuition: the observation of a fireball, a probable meteoroid impact, or space debris. This case is classified as Class B, like the probable observation of a fireball (meterooid impact, or space debris).

summary: Moon observation and probable sighting of a flying lantern.
description: person reports observing two unexplained phenomena on the same night. The first phenomenon observed (12:30 a.m. local time) likely corresponds to the sighting of the Moon in the east, 60% illuminated in a waning gibbous phase, described as an "orange semicircle on the horizon." The sky configuration at that time clearly shows the Moon in the observed sector. This case is classified as Class A, like the lunar observation. The second observation (1:23 a.m. local time) is independent, and the characteristics of the phenomenon suggest a sky lantern sighting.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a bright red luminous phenomenon: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern
description: On January 17, 2009, at 9:05 PM, a witness observed from their home the slow and silent movement of a bright red light above Grasse. The luminous phenomenon then ascended rapidly before disappearing into the sky. This observation, of low oddity but very thoroughly described by the witness, presents all the characteristics of a Thai lantern: red color, halo, movement with the wind, duration of a few minutes, on a Saturday (close to the Chinese New Year). This case is classified as "B," probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the slow movement of a lenticular-shaped white object: lack of information.
description: On January 15, 2009, at 10:15 AM, a witness observed the slow NE-SE movement of a lenticular-shaped white phenomenon. One hypothesis considered was that of a lenticular cloud. However, no investigation could be conducted due to a lack of information provided by the witness, despite a request from GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Astronomical Phenomena). This case is classified as "C" due to insufficient information.

summary: Observation of a point of light: lack of information.
description: On January 15, 2009, at 8:30 PM, a witness observed a very bright point in the sky. No investigation could be conducted because the witness did not respond to GEIPAN's requests. This case is classified as category C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation of the rapid and silent passage of a yellow-orange object. It fades and disappears.
description: On January 13, 2009, at 6:42 a.m., a motorist on the A20 motorway near Reaville saw an object through his windshield, moving quickly at an altitude of approximately 50 meters. The object was the size of a grapefruit and was yellow-orange in color. No sound was heard. The object disappeared, and no trail was observed. Despite our request to the witness, we received no police report. This case is classified as Category C due to lack of information.

summary: Bright orange object in photograph.
description: On January 11, 2009, at 8:55 PM, a photograph was taken from a balcony using a mobile phone. According to the witness, the moon is visible in the upper part of the image, and a streetlight is visible in the lower left part. However, an unidentified orange object appears on the right. No other information about the sighting was collected.

summary: Reflection of a light fixture in a photograph.
description: While trying to send a photograph of Marseille under the snow to her granddaughter, a witness noticed a luminous circular object in the photograph that she hadn't seen when the picture was taken on January 11, 2009, between 4 and 5 pm. It was actually the reflection of the kitchen neon light.

summary: Observation of a stationary round object with a change of colors: lack of information.
description: On January 9, 2009, at 9:29 PM, two witnesses observed a round object that appeared stationary in the sky, moving towards the south-southeast. One of the witnesses noted a color change. Only one witness statement, sent by email, was recorded by GEIPAN. The mentioned photograph was not attached to the email. The observation could correspond to the star Sirius, visible due southeast, whose color changes are characteristic. However, the lack of information gathered from the witness prevents this hypothesis from being fully confirmed. This case is classified as category C: lack of information.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon near a small plane at low altitude: lack of information.
description: On January 6, 2009, between 7:35 and 7:39 a.m., a witness observed a bright light on the side of an aircraft flying at low altitude. No other witness statements were collected. Due to the lack of a precise date for the initial observations, the absence of other witness statements, the lack of a fully completed questionnaire, and the absence of telephone contact, GEIPAN was unable to properly investigate this case. Furthermore, the late filing of the witness statement (four months after the event) makes aeronautical verification impossible. Pending any further witness statements, this case is classified as Class C due to lack of information.

summary: Observation in the sky of the rapid passage of two yellow-orange circles: lack of information.
description: On January 6, 2009, at 8:00 PM, a witness observed two yellow-orange circles moving rapidly in the sky from his home, heading towards Cambrai. The witness reported his observation by telephone to GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group); he refused to go to the police station. Due to the limited information provided by the witness, no hypothesis can be considered. This case is classified as category C: lack of information.

summary: Observation of the rapid fall of a point of light.
description: On January 3, 2009, at 8:10 PM, a driver and his passenger observed a very bright yellow light falling rapidly without any trail behind it. It quickly disappeared behind a hill. No unusual noise was heard. One possible explanation is the observation of atmospheric reentry, but in the absence of more precise information (particularly regarding the request for a report), this observation lacks sufficient information to allow for an investigation. The case is classified as "C".

summary: Possible sighting of luminous balloons illuminating a ski slope.
description: On January 1, 2009, at 8:00 PM, several people observed white lights moving from their balconies. These unusual lights on the other side of Lake Geneva intrigued the witnesses, who photographed them and examined them with binoculars. At 9:45 PM, the lights disappeared. With the help of daylight and the photographs, the witnesses precisely located the site of their observation: it was the Pic de Bore, specifically the location of a ski lift. The initial hypothesis put forward by GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie's Office for the Study of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena) was that these white lights may have been mistaken for the headlights of a snow groomer operating that evening. Witnesses later provided the likely explanation for the phenomenon: light balloons were used to illuminate the runway on the evening of January 1, 2009. Although this observation took place outside of French territory, the proximity of the French border (Haute-Savoie department) and the well-documented questionnaire encourage us to publish this testimony for informational purposes.

summary: Atmospheric return.
description: Numerous accounts of this atmospheric return on January 17, 2009 around 17:49 UTC have reached GEIPAN and various websites (see the REFORME network file Rentree Atm 17.01.2009-18h49locales.pdf).

summary: Observation of the unusual movement of a red luminous phenomenon in the sky: lack of information.
description: On January 1, 2009, at approximately 12:40 AM, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon moving through their bedroom window. The witness reported that a red point of light crossed the cloud cover, then descended slowly in a curve, following a horizontal trajectory before coming to a stop. It then diminished in intensity, appeared to rise back into the cloud cover, and disappeared. No other reports were received. GEIPAN (the French UFO research group) hypothesized that this observation corresponded to the launch of one or two distress flares launched for the New Year. This hypothesis is plausible and fairly consistent with the observation and the date of the event, but it is risky to confirm it due to a lack of photos, videos, or additional witness statements. This case is classified as Class C due to insufficient information.
